items.title: The domination order on tableaux, Garnir tableaux and bricks
items.statement:
Retain English Young diagrams and row-reading initial standard tableau t^mu. For a mu-tableau T let w_T t^mu=T. The STRONG Bruhat order on tableaux is S<=_B T iff w_S<=w_T in the permutation Bruhat order. For tableaux write S\unlhd T for S<=_B T and S\lhd T for strict order; partition dominance has its separately declared meaning. For row-strict S,T this is equivalent to the prefix shape of S DOMINATING the prefix shape of T for every prefix; it is distinct from weak Bruhat order and must not reverse this dominance direction. The transposition criterion is S=(a1 b1)...(am bm)T with an<bn and bn occupying an earlier row-reading node than an at each backward step.

For entries r,s in one component define r right-arrow_T s when they lie in the SAME row and s is strictly to the right; r down-arrow_T s when they lie in the SAME column and s is strictly below; and r northeast_T s when s is strictly ABOVE and strictly RIGHT of r. Southwest is the reverse northeast relation. A weak Bruhat graph edge T --r--> S requires both tableaux standard, S=s_r T, and r occupying an earlier row-reading node than r+1. Equivalently r+1 northeast_T r, or r is in an earlier component than r+1. In particular a same-column or same-row swap is NOT a standard edge. Terminal paths are directed paths ending at T.

The Garnir belt at (a,b,n) consists of the row-a tail from b and the row-(a+1) prefix through b. Its Garnir tableau is the maximal standard tableau in the strong Bruhat order agreeing with t^mu outside that belt. A horizontal brick is a string of consecutive entries along SAME-row right arrows. The following source facts are retained with these exact conventions: the transposition/prefix-shape criterion; the row-strictness of a vertical swap and its exceptional-prefix comparison; agreement outside the Garnir belt for lower tableaux; and the four terminal alternatives for a horizontal or vertical consecutive pair. For a horizontal pair the last alternative is T=t^mu; for a vertical pair it is the corresponding Garnir tableau. These finite combinatorial facts are proved in the strategy. No choice.
items.strategy: Permutation Bruhat order is characterized by successive inversions of transpositions with the larger entry in an earlier position; placing these entries in row-reading positions gives the transposition criterion. For row-strict tableaux count the entries <=a in each row: the Bruhat rank inequalities are exactly dominance of their prefix row-count shapes, with S dominating T when w_S<=w_T. This proves the prefix criterion and its direction (the row-reading initial tableau is Bruhat-minimal and has dominant prefixes). A consecutive swap is standard exactly for strict northeast/southwest positions or different components; same-row and same-column pairs violate row/column increase. Combine this with earlier row-reading position to obtain the directed edge criterion. For a vertical consecutive swap, only prefix a=r changes; row-strictness is immediate and the exceptional-prefix comparison follows by moving its box between those two rows. Sorting each row converts the same transposition criterion to the row-strict Bruhat comparison. A tableau below a Garnir tableau can change only positions within its belt: outside row prefixes coincide, so the same rank inequalities force those entries to remain fixed. For a consecutive horizontal pair test, in order, existence of a distant terminal interchange preserving the pair, then the two adjacent terminal paths (r,r+1) and (r,r-1). If none exists, the positions r-1,...,1 and r+2,...,d are forced into row-reading order, hence T=t^mu. The identical test for a vertical pair forces exactly the maximal belt filling if none of the first three alternatives holds. This supplies the local terminal reductions used by the two-part graded-Specht induction; bricks are horizontal, not vertical chains. Actual BKW §§3.2–3.4 source proof and positional conditions checked, no finite sample computation substitutes for the general criterion. No choice.

items.title: Generic nondegenerate local inverse tables on integer colors
items.statement:
Work over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, with $q\in k^\times$ of infinite multiplicative order, integer colors, and the arrows $a\to a+1$. On any finite permutation-stable set of color words, complete the dot ring at the zero dots. The completed local affine Hecke presentation at spectral words $(q^{i_1},\ldots,q^{i_d})$ and the completed type-$A_\infty$ KLR presentation have mutually inverse changes of generators below. This is a local statement; it does not assert cyclotomic support, a tower comparison, or a Specht dictionary.

Write $x=q^a(1-u)$, $z=q^b(1-v)$ and set
$$P_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1&a=b,\\(1-q)/(1-x/z)&a\ne b,\end{cases}$$
$$Q_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1-q+qv-u&a=b,\\-q^a/(x-z)&a=b+1,\\(x-qz)/(x-z)&a\ne b,\ a\ne b+1.\end{cases}$$
These are explicit, invertible, rank-independent power series over $k$; in particular the result applies over $\mathbb C$. Use $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}X_r$ on $e(i)$ and the source convention $\psi_r=-\tau_r$, where $\tau$ is the native crossing. The changes of generators are
$$\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})^{-1}e(i),$$
$$X_re(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i),\qquad T_re(i)=(\psi_rQ_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})-P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))e(i).$$
The quadratic polynomial is $K_{aa}=0$, $K_{a,a+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $K_{a+1,a}(u,v)=u-v$, and $K_{ab}=1$ otherwise. Equal-color dot-sliding constants for $\psi$ are $+1$. The braid order is $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$; on $(a,b,a)$ its value is $[K_{ab}(u,v)-K_{ab}(w,v)]/(w-u)$, hence respectively $+1,-1,0$ for forward, backward, nonadjacent colors.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The integer-color local presentations just stated. Their coefficient ring is the direct sum of one formal power-series ring per color word; no finite-$e$ definition or comparison theorem is being instantiated. In the Hecke presentation the spectral idempotents are the projections to these local rings. Multiplication by $X_r$ on its $i$-summand is $q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. The usual affine Hecke relations are $T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q$, $T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1}$, and the braid and distant commutation relations.

## Proof

**Given:** The displayed presentations and the formal series $P,Q$.

1.1 All coefficients are legal. For $a\ne b$, $x-z$ has constant $q^a-q^b\ne0$. In the last case of $Q$, $x-qz$ has nonzero constant because $a\ne b+1$. In the backward case $-q^a/(x-z)$ is a unit. In the equal case $1-q\ne0$. Thus every denominator is a unit and each $Q$ is a unit. The formulas depend only on the adjacent pair, so they make sense in every rank and in every finite color window. [given, algebra]



1.2 Use an explicit polynomial representation. On the $i$-component let dots multiply, and let a permutation simultaneously permute coordinates and colors. With $\partial_r=(s_r-1)/(y_r-y_{r+1})$, define $\psi_r$ on an equal pair to be $\partial_r$; on an unequal source pair $(a,b)$ let its output in the swapped component be $h_{ab}(u,v)s_r$, where $h_{ab}(u,v)=v-u$ if $a=b+1$ and $h_{ab}=1$ otherwise. The equal-color quotient is a power series because the numerator vanishes on $u=v$. Its product rule is $\partial(fg)=\partial(f)g+(sf)\partial(g)$. Consequently $\partial v=u\partial+1$, $v\partial=\partial u+1$, and $\partial^2=0$. On unequal pairs the square is multiplication by $h_{ba}(u,v)h_{ab}(v,u)=K_{ab}(u,v)$. These computations verify all mixed and quadratic relations, including the native sign $\tau=-\psi$. [given, algebra]



2.1 Three distinct colors. In both three-crossing words the coefficient of the longest permutation is the product of the three pair factors, transported to the same coordinates. Each pair is crossed once. The factors commute and $s_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1s_2$, so the two words agree. This argument does not require nonadjacency; some of the factors can be linear. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.2 First two colors equal. For $(a,a,b)$ write $h=h_{ab}$. The left word is $h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2\partial_1$, and the right word is $\partial_2h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2$. The product of factors is invariant under swapping $v,w$, so its $\partial_2$ is zero. Also $\partial_2s_1s_2=s_1s_2\partial_1$ by conjugating the displayed quotient. The words agree. For $(a,b,b)$ the left word is $\partial_1h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1$, and the right word is $h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1\partial_2$. Here the product is invariant under swapping $u,v$, and $\partial_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1\partial_2$. This verifies the third color pattern separately. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.3 Outer colors equal. On $(a,b,a)$ with $a\ne b$, put $h=h_{ab}$ and $g=h_{ba}$. Expanding the one equal-color crossing gives left and right words $\frac{g(u,v)}{u-w}\bigl(h(v,w)s_1s_2s_1-h(v,u)\bigr),\qquad\frac{h(v,w)}{u-w}\bigl(g(u,v)s_2s_1s_2-g(w,v)\bigr).$ Their longest-permutation terms cancel. Their difference is $[K_{ab}(w,v)-K_{ab}(u,v)]/(u-w)$, the stated braid correction. This equals $1$ when $b=a+1$, $-1$ when $a=b+1$, and zero otherwise. Thus the apparent denominator cancels identically. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.4 All three colors equal. Put $D=(u-v)(u-w)(v-w)$. Expanding the quotients and collecting each of the six permutations gives $\partial_1\partial_2\partial_1=\partial_2\partial_1\partial_2=-D^{-1}\sum_{t\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(t)t.$ The numerator is alternating and hence divisible by each of the three pair differences, so this is an operator on power series. This explicitly supplies the all-equal case omitted as an exercise in the source. Together with steps 2.1–2.3 it proves all five braid patterns. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.5 Compute the Hecke generators in the same representation. At an output component set $U=X_r$, $V=X_{r+1}$. For unequal colors the swapped input series $Q$ times $h$ is $(qU-V)/(U-V)$: in the backward case $qU-V=q^a(v-u)$, and the swapped input series is $-q^a/(V-U)=q^a/(U-V)$, so multiplying by $h=v-u$ gives exactly the stated coefficient. In every other unequal case this is the last row of $Q$ directly. Also $-P=(1-q)V/(U-V)$. For equal colors, expand $\partial Q-1$; its permutation coefficient is $(1-q+qu-v)/(u-v)$ and its identity coefficient is $-(1-q)(1-v)/(u-v)$. Thus in every case $T_r=A(U,V)s_r+B(U,V),\qquad A(U,V)=\frac{qU-V}{U-V},\quad B(U,V)=\frac{(1-q)V}{U-V}.$ The equal-color poles cancel on power series, as follows already from $T=\partial Q-1$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]



3.1 Mixed and quadratic Hecke identities. Write $A_{ij}=A(X_i,X_j)$ and $B_{ij}=B(X_i,X_j)$. Direct common-denominator expansion gives $B_{ij}+B_{ji}=q-1$, $A_{ij}=q-B_{ij}$, and $A_{ij}A_{ji}=q+(q-1)B_{ij}-B_{ij}^2$. Squaring $A_{ij}s+B_{ij}$ therefore gives $(q-1)T+q$. The identity $TX_i-X_{i+1}T=(1-q)X_{i+1}$ follows by cancellation of its permutation term. Combining this identity with the quadratic identity gives $TX_iT=qX_{i+1}$. Distant commutations follow from disjoint variables. [step 2.5, algebra]



4.1 The Hecke braid holds in every color pattern, including all equal. Set $c=q-1$. Clearing the three pair denominators gives the rational identity $B_{13}(c-B_{12}-B_{23})+B_{12}B_{23}=0$. The coefficients of the longest permutation, $s_1s_2$, and $s_2s_1$ in $T_1T_2T_1$ are $A_{12}A_{13}A_{23}$, $A_{12}A_{13}B_{23}$, and $B_{12}A_{23}A_{13}$; the right word has the same coefficients. The $s_1$ coefficients are $A_{12}(B_{13}B_{21}+B_{12}B_{23})$ and $A_{12}B_{23}B_{13}$; the displayed identity makes them equal. The $s_2$ comparison is its transposed version. The identity coefficients differ by $(B_{12}-B_{23})\bigl(B_{13}(c-B_{12}-B_{23})+B_{12}B_{23}\bigr)=0.$ This uses the quadratic product identity of step 3.1. These are all six permutations, so the braid is proved. It is a rational identity before any color specialization; the equal-color operators preserve power series by step 2.5. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]



5.1 These operator checks imply presentation identities, rather than identities on a possibly nonfaithful module. For Hecke coefficients the relation is $T_rf=(s_rf)T_r+B(X_r,X_{r+1})(f-s_rf)$. It follows first on the Laurent generators from the affine mixed relation, then on products by its product rule, and on formal local coefficients by continuity. At equal colors $f-s_rf$ is divisible by $X_r-X_{r+1}$; at unequal colors that denominator is a unit. This also gives the spectral-idempotent relation by applying the same formula to the local projections. For KLR use its displayed divided-difference product rule. Thus in either presentation coefficients can be moved past crossings. A crossing word reduces to a chosen reduced word for a permutation: delete adjacent repeated simple reflections using the quadratic relation, and change reduced words using commuting and three-term braid moves. For KLR the braid correction has fewer crossings. Induction on crossing length therefore spans the algebra by coefficient multiples of one chosen word per permutation. The elementary adjacent-transposition sorting algorithm supplies the requisite Coxeter reductions. In the rational crossed-product action, each reduced word has a nonzero coefficient of its own permutation; all other terms have shorter permutation length. Distinct permutations are linearly independent over the rational function field: in a minimal nonzero relation of automorphisms, apply it to $fg$ and subtract one automorphism's value on $f$ times its application to $g$; choose a coordinate $f$ moved differently by two permutations to obtain a shorter relation, a contradiction. Color words in different output components are already independent. Hence the spanning words are independent and both actions are faithful. The argument extends to formal coefficients using their fraction fields and the same finite spanning words. [step 1.2, step 2.4, step 4.1, algebra]



6.1 Both directions and both composites. In the faithful KLR action, steps 2.5–4.1 prove the Hecke relations of the displayed inverse generators. In the faithful local Hecke action, solving step 2.5 gives precisely the polynomial crossings of step 1.2, whose relations were proved in steps 1.2 and 2.1–2.4. Since $Q$ is a unit, the two operator subalgebras generated by coefficients and their respective crossings coincide. Thus the presentations are isomorphic. On idempotents and dots the two composites are the identity by the spectral decomposition and $X_r=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. On crossings the composite is $(\psi_rQ-P+P)Q^{-1}=\psi_r$; on Hecke crossings it is $(T_r+P)Q^{-1}Q-P=T_r$. These are ordered products; no coefficient has been commuted past a crossing. This completes the local inverse comparison in both directions. [step 1.1, step 5.1, construct] ∎

items.statement: Let $A_{\mathbb Z}$ be a finite free unital integer algebra with $A_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes A_{\mathbb Z}$, and let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field. Suppose a finite-dimensional graded cyclic $A_K$-module $S_K$, with specified homogeneous generator $z_K$, is obtained from a homogeneous integer cyclic presentation $S_{\mathbb Z}=A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ by scalar extension, carrying $1+I_{\mathbb Z}$ to $z_K$. Suppose $S_K$ has a nonzero simple head $D_K$, with its specified grading normalization. Then the pair consisting of $D_K$ and the line spanned by the image $v$ of $z_K$ descends to $\mathbb Q$. More precisely there is a graded quotient $D_{\mathbb Q}$ of $S_{\mathbb Q}$ and $v_{\mathbb Q}\ne0$ such that $K\otimes D_{\mathbb Q}\cong D_K$ carries $1\otimes v_{\mathbb Q}$ to $v$. Consequently $A_{\mathbb Z}v$ is free of rank $\dim_KD_K$. If $D_K$ is absolutely simple, every nonzero quotient map from the specified $S_K$ to the fixed normalized $D_K$ has generator image on this same line, up to $K^\times$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[thm-jacobson-radical-is-nilpotent-and-the-quotient-is-semisimple]] gives a nilpotent radical and semisimple quotient for every finite-dimensional algebra.

[F2] [[thm-wedderburn-artin-theorem]] and [[thm-simple-modules-over-semisimple-rings]] describe semisimple finite-dimensional algebras and their simples.

[F3] [[thm-schurs-lemma-for-modules]] applies to simple modules.

[F4] [[thm-irreducible-quotient-adjoins-a-root]] constructs a finite root field for a monic irreducible polynomial. A nonconstant characteristic polynomial has a monic irreducible factor by finite induction on degree.

[A1] The integer presentation is an explicit prerequisite, not asserted here for the existing Hecke Specht construction. Its identification must preserve the specified generator.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement and F1–F4. All constructions involve finite-dimensional spaces and finite root fields; no Axiom of Choice is used.

1.1 We prove the regular-trace radical criterion directly over ANY characteristic-zero field $F$, without a splitting field or algebraic closure. Let $B$ be a finite-dimensional $F$-algebra and $\beta_B(a,b)=\operatorname{Tr}_F(L_{ab}:B\to B)$. Every element of $J(B)$ is orthogonal to $B$, because its product with any element lies in the nilpotent radical and hence has nilpotent left multiplication and zero trace. Choose a finite composition series of the left regular module. F1–F2 give $B/J(B)\cong\prod_iM_{n_i}(D_i)$, where each $D_i$ is a finite-dimensional division algebra over $F$; every simple composition factor is its column module $D_i^{n_i}$. Additivity of trace along the composition series shows that on this quotient the pairing is $\sum_i m_i\operatorname{Tr}_F(\rho_i(X_iY_i):D_i^{n_i}\to D_i^{n_i})$, where $m_i$ is the positive integer multiplicity of the column module in the regular composition series. Every $m_i$ is positive because the regular quotient already contains the corresponding column module. For a nonzero entry $x_{ab}$ of a block $X_i$, choose $Y_i$ with its only nonzero entry $(b,a)$ equal to $x_{ab}^{-1}$, and set all other blocks of $Y$ to zero. The product $X_iY_i$ has exactly one nonzero diagonal entry, namely $1$ at position $a$. On the $F$-space $D_i^{n_i}$, its action therefore has trace $\dim_F D_i$; off-diagonal blocks contribute no trace. The full pairing on this $Y$ is $m_i\dim_FD_i\ne0$ in characteristic zero. Thus the quotient pairing is nondegenerate and $\ker\beta_B=J(B)$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Apply step 1.1 over $F=\mathbb Q$ and $F=K$. The regular multiplication and trace matrices for $A_K$ are scalar extensions of those for $A_{\mathbb Q}$. Row reduction of a finite matrix commutes with field extension, so the kernels satisfy $\ker\beta_{A_K}=K\otimes\ker\beta_{A_{\mathbb Q}}$. The radical criterion gives $J(A_K)=K\otimes J(A_{\mathbb Q})$. This argument applies equally to nonsplit division factors and needs no separable splitting theorem. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Put $S_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes S_{\mathbb Z}$ and $D_{\mathbb Q}=S_{\mathbb Q}/J(A_{\mathbb Q})S_{\mathbb Q}$. Tensoring quotient presentations is right exact and $K/\mathbb Q$ is flat, so $K\otimes D_{\mathbb Q}=S_K/J(A_K)S_K$. This last quotient is precisely the semisimple head: $A_K/J(A_K)$ is semisimple, so the quotient is semisimple, while every simple quotient kills $J(A_K)S_K$. Equivalently, intersections of maximal submodules equal $J(A_K)S_K$, since the intersection of the maximal submodules of a finite semisimple module is zero. The assumed head is simple, so this quotient is $D_K$. Its rational precursor is nonzero and simple: a proper nonzero rational submodule would remain proper and nonzero after faithful scalar extension. [F1, F2, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 The radical of a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-graded algebra is homogeneous. Indeed all scaling automorphisms $a_d\mapsto t^d a_d$ preserve its characteristic ideal $J$, for $t\in\mathbb Q^\times$. If $a=\sum_{d\in E}a_d\in J$ with finite degree set $E$, take $t=2^j$ for $j=0,\ldots,|E|-1$. The resulting coefficient matrix $((2^d)^j)_{j,d}$ is Vandermonde in the pairwise distinct rational numbers $2^d$, hence invertible; each $a_d$ is a rational linear combination of elements of $J$. Thus $J(A_{\mathbb Q})S_{\mathbb Q}$ is homogeneous and $D_{\mathbb Q}$ has the required quotient grading. Put $v_{\mathbb Q}=z_{\mathbb Q}+J(A_{\mathbb Q})S_{\mathbb Q}$. It is nonzero: otherwise cyclicity would force $D_{\mathbb Q}=0$. The scalar-extension quotient isomorphism preserves the generator, and hence its image is exactly $v$, including its degree. Any prescribed normalization shift is imposed simultaneously on both modules. [step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 The orbit $A_{\mathbb Z}v_{\mathbb Q}$ is generated as an abelian group by the images of a finite integer basis of $A_{\mathbb Z}$. It is torsion-free because it is a subgroup of a rational vector space. Its rational span is $D_{\mathbb Q}$, by cyclicity, so its rank equals $\dim_{\mathbb Q}D_{\mathbb Q}=\dim_KD_K$. The generator-preserving scalar-extension isomorphism identifies this orbit with $A_{\mathbb Z}v$. A finitely generated torsion-free abelian group is free, which proves the lattice assertion. [step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.2 If a fixed normalized $D_K$ is absolutely simple, a nonzero map $S_K\to D_K$ is surjective and kills the radical. Since the head is already the simple $D_K$, such maps factor through its canonical quotient and differ by an invertible endomorphism of $D_K$. This endomorphism $f$ is scalar using a finite root-field construction. Its nonconstant characteristic polynomial has a monic irreducible factor; by F4 the corresponding quotient field $L/K$ supplies a root $\alpha$. The matrix $f_L-\alpha I$ has zero determinant and hence a nonzero kernel. Absolute simplicity makes $D_L$ simple, so this commuting endomorphism must be zero. Thus $f_L=\alpha I$, and any diagonal entry of the original $K$-matrix shows $\alpha\in K$. Thus every allowed generator image is a scalar multiple of the constructed image, and scaling the lattice preserves freeness and rank. No claim concerning an arbitrary vector in $D_K$ was used. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.statement:
Let $k$ have characteristic zero, let $\xi\in k^\times$ have infinite
multiplicative order, and fix a finite integral multicharge
$m_1,\ldots,m_\ell$. Write $S=\{m_j:1\le j\le\ell\}$.
Use the arbitrary-base presentations of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] to define
$H_d^{\deg}$ by $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$ and $H_d^{\xi}$ by
$\prod_j(X_1-\xi^{m_j})=0$.
For $d>0$, every nonzero joint generalized weight in the regular module has
labels $\nu\in\mathbb Z^d$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ respectively
$\xi^{\nu_r}$, and
$$\min_{s\in S}|\nu_r-s|\le d-1.$$
Thus both algebras have finite joint spectral decompositions defined over $k$.

Use the directed line $i\to i+1$ on $\mathbb Z$, with $d_i=1$,
$Q_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $Q_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v$ and $Q_{ij}=1$ for
$|i-j|>1$. Define the rank-$d$ cyclotomic KLR algebra as the direct sum of its
finite-content presentations, with first-strand exponents
$\lambda_i=\#\{j:m_j=i\}$. Every nonzero word idempotent satisfies the same
bound, so this rank algebra is a finite sum of finite-dimensional graded
content algebras. Any interval containing
$[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]$ gives exactly the same rank-$d$ algebra;
enlarging it introduces only zero word idempotents. Rank zero is $k$.
At level zero every positive rank is zero. This lemma supplies support and
finite windows; it asserts no Hecke--KLR isomorphism or basis correspondence.

No cyclic wraparound or reduction of integer colors is used. [A1, A2, algebra]

2.1 On a first color $i$, write the degenerate cyclotomic polynomial as $f(i+y)=y^{\lambda_i}U_i(y)$, where $U_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(i-m_j+y)$. Its constant term is nonzero in characteristic zero. In the other branch $g(\xi^i(1-y))=(-\xi^i)^{\lambda_i}y^{\lambda_i}V_i(y)$, where $V_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(\xi^i-\xi^{m_j}-\xi^iy)$. Infinite multiplicative order makes its constant term nonzero. Both auxiliary factors are units after nilpotent evaluation. Thus the Hecke cyclotomic relation on each projector is equivalent to $y_1^{\lambda_i}e(i,\ldots)=0$. If $\lambda_i=0$, the unit polynomial kills the entire projector. This proves the cyclotomic factorization and descent in both directions. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Denote the descended reverse map by $\sigma_d:H_d\to R_d^\lambda$. On $e_R(\nu)R_d^\lambda$, each $\sigma_d(x_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\nu_r$, or $\sigma_d(X_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\xi^{\nu_r}$. Distinct colors have distinct values, and the orthogonal word idempotents sum to one. The simultaneous primary projector is therefore precisely left multiplication by $e_R(\nu)$. The Hecke polynomial projector maps to this idempotent: its Chinese-remainder polynomial is one modulo the corresponding primary factors and zero modulo all other factors. Hence $\sigma_d(e_H(\nu))=e_R(\nu)$. The forward map already sends $e_R(\nu)$ to $e_H(\nu)$. [A1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Both composites fix the word projectors by step 3.1 and the dots by direct substitution $x_r-\nu_r=y_r$, or $1-\xi^{-\nu_r}X_r=y_r$. On a word, the crossing composite is $(\psi_rq_{ab}-p_{ab}+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$, or $(\psi_rQ_{ab}-P_{ab}+P_{ab})Q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$. Conversely the Hecke composite sends $s_re_H(\nu)$ to $((s_r+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}q_{ab}-p_{ab})e_H(\nu)=s_re_H(\nu)$; the formula with $T,P,Q$ is identical. The polynomial generators are fixed, and the units $X_r^{-1}$ are fixed because inverses are unique. Thus the homomorphisms are inverse on every generator, without commuting a crossing through its series. [step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For ranks through $D>0$ at positive level use the common interval $W_D=[\min S-D,\max S+D]\cap\mathbb Z$. It contains the support through rank $D$ and one unused ghost color beyond each endpoint of $B_D$. A crossing permutes existing colors and never creates one; nevertheless these endpoint colors keep every boundary edge of a surviving color represented by the integer-line convention. For operations reaching rank $D+t$, use $W_{D+t}$, and enlarge further to contain any specified color and its neighbors. All extra word idempotents vanish by [A1]. Since [A2] fixes the same series for each ordered pair in every interval, evaluation on surviving words is unchanged by enlargement. The resulting maps are independent of windows and glue across all finite rank bounds. [A1, A2, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 Let $\iota_H:H_d\to H_{d+1}$ send each existing Hecke generator to the generator with the same index. It is a homomorphism because all rank-$d$ relations, including the first-strand relation, hold in rank $d+1$. Its spectral projector satisfies $\iota_H(e_H(\nu))=\sum_a e_H(\nu,a)$: the first $d$ polynomial generators give a representation of $H_d$ on the rank-$d+1$ regular module, so their primary projector is the sum of exactly these joint projectors. Prefixes violating rank-$d$ support are zero by [A1] applied to this representation. This argument also holds for $d=0$, where the empty projector is one. [A1, given, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Define $\iota_R=\sigma_{d+1}\iota_H\phi_d$. The established inverse maps make this a homomorphism. Steps 3.1 and 6.1 give $\iota_R(e_R(\nu))=\sum_a e_R(\nu,a)$. The unchanged polynomial generators give the usual prefix dots. For $r<d$, the rank-independent pair series in [A2] and cancellation in step 4.1 give $\iota_R(\psi_re_R(\nu))=\sum_a\psi_re_R(\nu,a)$. These are exactly the standard right-appending KLR maps, so the individually constructed isomorphisms commute with the actual tower maps. Injectivity of the tower maps is neither needed nor inferred. [A2, step 4.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 Put $\epsilon_i^R=\sum_\nu e_R(\nu,i)$ in rank $d+1$, and define $\epsilon_i^H$ by the analogous spectral sum. Step 3.1 gives $\phi_{d+1}(\epsilon_i^R)=\epsilon_i^H$. Each last-color projector commutes with every prefix generator, since prefix crossings permute only the first $d$ colors and prefix dots preserve all colors. On left modules color restriction is $N\mapsto\epsilon_iN$, with the rank-$d$ action through its prefix map. Color induction is $M\mapsto A_{d+1}\epsilon_i\otimes_{A_d}M$. Step 7.1 identifies both prefix actions, and the algebra isomorphism identifies these induction bimodules on both sides. Explicitly $a\epsilon_i\otimes m\mapsto\phi_{d+1}(a)\epsilon_i\otimes m$ is a balanced bijection, with inverse obtained from $\sigma_{d+1}$. Restriction agrees by the same projector equality. These formulas are natural in module maps. [step 3.1, step 7.1, construct]

9.1 Composing the two comparisons through the same $R_d^\lambda$ proves the claimed degenerate/nondegenerate tower equivalence. Naturality from step 8.1 intertwines repeated induction and restriction, while step 5.1 covers every specified finite rank cut. At level zero use the identity on rank zero and the unique maps between zero algebras in positive rank; the sole map from rank zero to rank one is the map to zero, and all positive-rank functors vanish. Thus all ranks and levels are included. Every conclusion remains conditional on [A1] and [A2]; no local table identity or based theorem has been established by this gluing proof. [A1, step 5.1, step 8.1] ∎

items.title: Extremal word characters detect normalized cyclotomic simple labels
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic KLR module M over any field, choose a word by successive maximal last-color blocks i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}. There is exactly one normalized simple shift orbit S_c contributing to that word; its right crystal label is c=tilde f_{i_s}^{r_s}...tilde f_{i_1}^{r_1}u_Lambda. Its word graded dimension is product_a [r_a]_{i_a}!, and [M:S_c]_v equals gdim e(word)M divided by that product. All other simple orbits have zero word space. Consequently graded word characters are injective on G0. If two fields have modules with the same word character, their extremal words and detected canonical B(Lambda) labels coincide. No one-dimensional word-space assertion is made. Choice is inherited only through the existing abstract crystal identification.
items.strategy:
Let M be a finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic module. Choose a nonzero word by successively maximizing the last constant-color block, then the preceding block after restricting that maximum, until the vacuum is reached. Write the resulting word as i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}, adjacent colors distinct. Restriction to a word idempotent is exact. Every simple constituent with nonzero word space must have precisely the same first maximal last-block length: a shorter length gives zero, a longer length would contradict maximality for M. The actual maximal-tail supplier identifies the full maximal restriction of this simple with N tensor L(i_s^{r_s}), where N is simple with zero residual i_s-tail. Repeat on N and on the corresponding exact restriction of M. At the end N is the unique vacuum simple. Reconstruct using the actual unique-head induction supplier. Hence exactly ONE simple shift orbit can contribute at the chosen word. Its crystal label is obtained by the same successive right-induction powers from the vacuum, so is field independent under the native11 canonical B(Lambda) identification.

For the normalized simple S in that orbit, maximal restriction is normalized N tensor normalized L(i^r): restriction commutes with finite vector duality, the two factors are absolutely simple, and their unique self-dual normalizations force the remaining shift to be zero. The normalized rank-r nil-Hecke simple has graded dimension [r]_i!, by the actual polynomial/corner calculation with shift -d_i binomial(r,2). Iterating gives gdim e(word)S=product_a [r_a]_{i_a}!. Therefore the coefficient of [S] in [M] is gdim e(word)M divided by this nonzero product. No one-dimensional Hom or semisimplicity shortcut is used. The same exact argument, ordering maximal tuples, shows that characters of normalized simples are linearly independent: choose the lexicographically maximal tuple with nonzero coefficient and evaluate its extremal word, then remove it. Thus graded word character equality implies G0 equality, over each original field.

 For character injectivity, realize the finite set of simple orbits appearing in a virtual relation as their direct sum, choose an extremal word as above, and evaluate the relation: exactly one orbit contributes, with its nonzero factorial polynomial. Its Laurent coefficient is zero. Remove it and repeat on the remaining finite set. This proves injectivity without assuming the relation is a module.

items.title: Standard Fock vectors expand in the upper global basis
items.statement:
Use the symmetric model $M_\mu=|\mu'\rangle$ of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]], the
basic field subspace $V$ of the vacuum Fock space spanned by the restricted
lower vectors $G(\lambda)=\sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)M_\mu$ of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]],
and the bilinear form $B(M_\mu,M_\nu)=\delta_{\mu,\nu}$. Define the **standard
coordinate functional** $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ in the restricted integral
weight dual of the lower lattice by
$\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)=B(x,M_\mu)$. The restriction of $B$ to $V$ is
nondegenerate; identify its field dual with $V$ via $B$ and denote by
$\pi(M_\mu)$ the vector representing $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$, equivalently the
$B$-orthogonal projection of $M_\mu$ onto $V$. This is the definition of $\pi$
used below, not an undeclared projection from a generic upper-basis definition.
If $G^*(\lambda)$ is the $B$-dual upper vector, then
$$\operatorname{Std}_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)=\sum_{\lambda\ \mathrm{restricted}} d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\,G^*(\lambda).$$
At each content the restricted $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda$ form an $A$-basis of
the upper dual lattice, by the restricted dominance-unitriangular coefficient
minor. The full family of raw $M_\mu$ is the basis of the ambient standard
lattice; the full projected family $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ is generally
redundant. The projection $\pi$ need not land in the lower integral lattice. In
$e=2$ one has $G_{11}=M_{11}+qM_2$ and
$G_{11}^*=(M_{11}+qM_2)/(1+q^2)$, exhibiting the possible field denominator.
The sums at fixed content are finite. Choice is inherited only from the
declared global-basis suppliers.
items.strategy: Use the true symmetric transition support: off-diagonal standard shapes dominate lower labels. The restricted minor is finite unitriangular and has a finite polynomial inverse; the particular ambient Gram matrix is invertible because H(0)=I. Restrict the standard-coordinate functional to the basic lower lattice, obtaining A-valued coordinates and its unique representing vector in the basic subspace. The local normalized form identification makes the inverse-Gram family the transported upper global basis, so finite dual-pairing computations give Std_mu=pi(M_mu)=sum_lambda d(lambda,mu)G^*(lambda). The restricted minor proves the restricted standard functionals are an upper integral-dual basis, while the full projected family can be redundant and lower integrality can fail. Contravariance makes the basic orthogonal complement stable, hence pi intertwines the action; transposing diagrams yields the canonical removal recursion. Choice is only inherited.

items.title: Graded module and projective Grothendieck groups of the KLR and Hecke towers
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}R_\alpha$ be a tower of
finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras with local units
$e(\alpha)$: every finite root-supported element has a unit given by the sum of its finitely many sector units, each
$R_\alpha$ a direct summand and $R_0=k$. Define
$$K_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),\qquad G_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),$$
the restricted direct sums of the blockwise Grothendieck groups of
[[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]]:
$K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finitely generated graded left
$R_\alpha$-projectives modulo split exact sequences
([[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]]) and
$G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finite-dimensional graded left $R_\alpha$-modules
modulo short exact sequences. Both are modules over
$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ by $q[M]:=[M\{1\}]$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]), and inside each
finite-dimensional block the shift-orbit bases of
[[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]] hold. The
Cartan homomorphism $c:K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(R)$, $[P]\mapsto[P]$, is
$A$-linear. The forgetful maps $\zeta$ to the ungraded groups $K_0(R)$,
$G_0(R)$ are additive and satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$. The groups $K_0^{\rm gr}$ and
$G_0^{\rm gr}$ are DIFFERENT objects and are never identified.

**The two towers used below.** (i) For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic
quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] at the
level-one weight $\Lambda_0$ of
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]], put
$R^\Lambda_\alpha=R^\Lambda(\alpha)$; every block is finite dimensional and has
the homogeneous symmetrizing functional of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric`, with
grading shifts as in [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. (ii) For
the cyclotomic Hecke tower $H^{\Lambda}:=\bigoplus_\alpha H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
`def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras` with the block decomposition
of `def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks`, fix an
admissible local normalising series and transport the homogeneous KLR
decomposition through the blockwise isomorphism of
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism`, as in
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`; the induced
transport identifies $K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\cong K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)$
as $A$-modules and similarly for $G_0^{\rm gr}$, compatibly with $\zeta$ and
with the Cartan homomorphisms. Every class has finite root support, so the
direct sums are restricted.

No choice principle is used in this definition.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $k$, a tower $R=\bigoplus_\alpha R_\alpha$ of
finite-dimensional graded algebras with local units over the standard
cyclotomic quotient at $\Lambda_0$, and the Hecke tower $H^\Lambda$ with an
admissible local normalising series. All modules are left modules and all maps
preserve degree.

[F1] For a finite-dimensional graded algebra $A$, the groups
$G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$, the shift action
$v^r[M]=[M\{r\}]$ and the graded Cartan homomorphism
$c_A^{\mathrm{gr}}:[P]\mapsto[P]$ are those of
[[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]]; shift is
invertible and composes by addition of degrees, and $c_A^{\mathrm{gr}}$ is
$\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-linear.

[F2] The graded-simple shift orbits and the classes of chosen graded
projective covers form $\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$-bases of
$G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ and $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A)$ for every finite-dimensional
graded $k$-algebra $A$, with no positivity assumption
([[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]]).

[F3] A finitely generated graded projective module is a finite direct sum of
finite-dimensional indecomposable graded projectives
([[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]]), and internal shift is
the degreewise operation $M\{r\}_d=M_{d-r}$ of
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

[F4] The cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ at a dominant integral weight
is the quotient of the KLR algebra $R(\beta)$ by the two-sided ideal generated
by the first-strand cyclotomic elements, with local units $e(\beta)$ acting as
the identity on their summand
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]), and its grading is the
diagrammatic grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

[F5] Every block $R^\Lambda(\alpha)$ of the standard level-one cyclotomic
quotient is finite dimensional and carries a homogeneous symmetrizing
functional (the blockwise finite-dimensionality and symmetry statement of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric`), and
the blockwise isomorphism of
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism` matches each Hecke
block with its KLR block, the transported grading being supplied by
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Restricted sums are A-modules.** Each summand $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R_\alpha)$ is a module over $A$ by $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$, and shift by an integer $r$ sends a class concentrated in degree $\alpha$ to the same root degree $\alpha$, because internal shift changes only the internal grading and not the idempotent label [F1, F3]. Hence every finite $A$-combination of classes lives in finitely many root summands and the restricted direct sums are $A$-modules; the local units $e(\alpha)$ make each $R_\alpha$ a unital subalgebra and annihilate the other summands, so the restricted direct sum is well defined and no infinite-support class is introduced. [F1, F3]

1.2 **The maps c and zeta.** On each block the ungraded forgetful map sends a graded projective class to its underlying projective class and a graded module class to its underlying module class; it is additive, well defined on the defining relations, and satisfies $\zeta(q[M])=\zeta([M\{1\}])=[M]_{\rm ungr}=\zeta([M])$ [F1]. The graded Cartan homomorphism is the sum of the blockwise maps $[P]\mapsto[P]$, which are $A$-linear because including a projective into the module category commutes with internal shift; compatibility with $\zeta$ is immediate from the definitions. [F1]

1.3 **The KLR tower.** For the standard level-one cyclotomic quotient every block $R^\Lambda(\alpha)$ is finite dimensional and carries the homogeneous symmetrizing functional of [F5], so the shift-orbit bases of [F2] apply blockwise without any positivity hypothesis [F4, F5]. Since the root degree is additive, a finite combination of block classes has finite support and belongs to the restricted direct sum. [F2, F4, F5]

1.4 **Transport to the Hecke tower.** For each residue-content block, the blockwise theorem of [F5] gives a graded $k$-algebra isomorphism $\varphi_\alpha:H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda(\alpha)$ matched with the chosen admissible normalising series, and the inherited grading of [F5] makes $\varphi_\alpha$ homogeneous. Restriction of scalars along $\varphi_\alpha$ sends graded $R^\Lambda(\alpha)$-modules to graded $H^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules and is an equivalence of graded module categories: it is exact because it is induced by an algebra isomorphism, it preserves finite-dimensional modules, and it preserves projectives because restriction along an isomorphism has the exact quasi-inverse given by restriction along $\varphi_\alpha^{-1}$, which is also exact. Hence it induces group isomorphisms $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)\cong K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)\cong G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)$; these are $A$-linear because a homogeneous isomorphism carries $M\{1\}$ to $M\{1\}$, and they intertwine the Cartan maps and the forgetful maps $\zeta$ with the ungraded identifications. [F1, F3, F5]

2.1 **The groups remain distinct and no choice is used.** The identification $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R)\cong K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)$ is only a module transport inside one of the two groups; the Cartan homomorphism $c$ and the forgetful $\zeta$ are not inverted or identified, and no statement of the definition equates $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}$ with $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}$. All constructions use the finite block decompositions, the local units, and the explicit homogeneous algebra isomorphisms, so no choice principle is invoked. [F1, F5, given] ∎

items.title: The nondegenerate root-of-unity level-one Hecke regime
items.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary Dipper–James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Define $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block. At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]] identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains outside the present nondegenerate regime.

items.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The ordinary dictionary uses the actual universal module-and-form comparison [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], not a rename of a cellular module. Its Laurent-unit form factor preserves radicals, including zero quotients, and gives $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}\cong(D_{\rm M}^{\lambda})^{\theta}$; apply the involution again. Right-to-left conversion sends $h\cdot m=m h^*$, and commutation $\theta *=*\theta$ preserves the same pullback dictionary. On the finite level-one tower $X_j=\xi^{1-j}T_{j-1}\cdots T_1^2\cdots T_{j-1}$. Applying $\theta(T_r)=-\xi T_r^{-1}$ to this palindrome gives $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$: the $2j-2$ signs cancel and the scalar is $\xi^{j-1}$. items.title: The graded Cartan pairing between projective and module classes
items.statement:
In the situation and notation of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], for each root degree $\alpha$, finite-dimensional graded left $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules $M$ and finitely generated graded projective $P$ put $$h_\alpha(P,M):=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}(P,M)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}q^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha,d}(P,M)\in A .$$ By [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] (whose finite-dimensional hypotheses hold blockwise) this descends to an $A$-sesquilinear pairing $$h:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\times G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow A,$$ with the twist $q\mapsto q^{-1}$: $h(q^r[P],q^s[M])=q^{s-r}h([P],[M])$. In particular $h^0(P,S):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)$ is the degree-zero part. The pairing on the Hecke side is the transported pairing of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]. Also fix the two dualities used below: the descended anti-involution $\psi$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] with its finite-module duality $D_\psi$ and finite-projective duality $\#$, both shift-reversing and involutive on their domains; and the convention that a simple module or projective cover is called *normalized* when it is fixed (not merely fixed up to shift) by the relevant duality and, for a cover, when $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$.

No perfectness, nondegeneracy or $A$-self-duality is asserted in this definition; those are supplied by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] and its transported form on the Hecke side.

items.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
items.statement:
Work in the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition
$\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be
the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with
$S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by
`thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular` $K(\mu)$ is a
two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is
defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module**
$$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$
a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) fix a reduced decomposition
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put
$z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov--Lauda presentation
of `def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras`. For a
removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]) define
$$d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$$
(equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and
define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by
$\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$,
$\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing
$d$.

The definition asserts, and
`thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis` on this page proves,
that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of
$S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading
recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell
module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting
its grading, `thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual`
identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape
independently defined ordinary Dipper--James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately,
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell` gives
$S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are
two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate
module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to
$\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary
form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The
labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted
here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The nondegenerate level-one regime with its partition parameters
$\mu$, $d=|\mu|$ and content $\alpha$, the Murphy cellular basis of the finite
type-$A$ Hecke algebra, and the KLR presentation of the block.

[F1] The regime supplies the field $F$, the parameter $\xi$, the level-one
weight, the Hecke and KLR towers, the blocks $H^\Lambda_\alpha$, the symmetric
residue convention and the independent grading variable $q$
([[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]).

[F2] The Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ and the cell/Specht modules of the
cyclotomic Hecke algebra are those of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]]; the
left module structure is obtained from the right cellular datum through the
star anti-involution.

[F3] Standard tableaux, their shapes, the row-reading initial tableau
$t^\mu$, removable and addable nodes, and the associated permutations $w_T$ are
as declared in [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]],
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]].

[F4] The sign automorphism $\theta$ is the involution of
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and $\theta$ commutes with
the star anti-involution.

[F5] The KLR generators, their grading and the degrees $\deg e(i)=0$,
$\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ are those of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The ideal and the cyclic generator.** The span $K(\mu)$ of the Murphy elements indexed by standard pairs of shape strictly dominating $\mu$ is a two-sided ideal by the cellularity theorem `thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular`, and the class $z_\mu=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is the canonical generator of the cell module [F2]. The left action is obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=mh^*$, so $S(\mu)=H^\Lambda_dz_\mu$ is a left module; no right module is identified with a left module without this conversion [F2]. [F2]

1.2 **The block and the basic parameters.** The content $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$ and the equation $d=|\mu|$ place $S(\mu)$ in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of the level-one Hecke algebra, because the Murphy basis is block-decomposed by residue content and the cell module of $\mu$ involves only the content $\alpha$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2]

1.3 **The vectors.** For each standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$; the elements $z_T=T_{w_T}z_\mu$ and $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ are defined by left multiplication in the Hecke and KLR presentations, and $T_{w_T}$ is independent of its Hecke reduced expression, whereas $\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ can depend on the chosen reduced word: the KLR braid relation has correction terms [F5]. The resulting family is defined for the selected reduced words, and the theorem of this page proves that the induced grading is well defined; no basis or homogeneity claim is made at this point [F5]. [F4, F5]

1.4 **The degree recursion is well defined.** For a standard tableau $T$ of size $d>0$, $T_{\le d-1}$ is a standard tableau of the smaller shape and the node $A$ of $T$ containing $d$ is removable in that shape, so the recursion $\deg(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ is a finite induction on $d$ with values in $\mathbb Z$ depending only on $T$ and $\mu$; the two equivalent expressions for $d_A(\lambda)$ agree in the symmetric residue convention of the regime [F1, F3]. [F1, F3]

2.1 **The ungraded comparisons and Choice.** Forgetting the grading, the star-contragredient duality of `thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual` identifies the left cell module with the same-shape Specht dual, and the signed-conjugate comparison of `thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell` gives $S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after conversion; since $\theta$ commutes with star by [F4], both comparisons keep their stated positions and neither asserts untwisted conjugate identification [F4]. Every construction selects finite sets of reduced decompositions and finite basis data, so no choice principle is used. [F2, F4, given] ∎

items.title: The integral form of the cyclotomic Hecke-KLR block
items.statement: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field in branch (C0) of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] and fix, for each residue content $\alpha$, the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}$, $\{y_r\}$, $\{\psi_r\}$ of the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], i.e. the $\rho_\alpha$-images of the KLR generators ([[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]), in a fixed admissible local normalising series. Define $$H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z):=\bigl\langle e(i),\ y_r,\ \psi_r\ \bigr\rangle_{\mathbb Z}\subseteq H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$$ to be the $\mathbb Z$-subring generated by them. It is the $\mathbb Z$-span of the same finite normal forms (in the Khovanov-Lauda generators) that span $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ over $K$, hence a free $\mathbb Z$-module and a lattice; the generator degrees give it a grading, and the base-change maps $$K\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(K),\qquad F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(F)$$ sending $1\otimes e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $1\otimes y_r\mapsto y_r$, $1\otimes\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$ are isomorphisms of graded algebras for every field $F$ of sub-branch (CP) with a primitive $e$-th root of unity, the second being the reduction modulo $p$. The direct sums over $\alpha$ give the integral form of the tower. No choice is used.
items.strategy: Use the exact integer type-A KLR presentation with generator images in each characteristic-zero sector. Integer PBW straightening spans its image by ordered dot monomials times crossing words and word idempotents. Dot nilpotence in the finite characteristic-zero standard cyclotomic quotient bounds every position; finitely many words give finitely many nonzero spanning monomials. Their Z-span is closed under integer straightening and is torsion-free inside the characteristic-zero algebra. First descend to Q: the map from the Q KLR presentation to the generator image becomes the actual BK isomorphism after extending to K; faithful field extension makes it an isomorphism already over Q. Thus the integer image is a full finite lattice in this Q-algebra, of rank equal to dim_K H_alpha(K), and K tensor this lattice is H_alpha(K). For EVERY content alpha at fixed rank the reduced named generators satisfy the integer relations and generate F tensor the lattice, giving a SURJECTION H_alpha(F) -> F tensor H_alpha(Z) via the actual field BK presentation. Consequently dim_F H_alpha(F) >= dim_K H_alpha(K) for every alpha, including zero sectors. Sum over all finitely many rank-d contents: both total dimensions equal ell^d d! by the late field basis theorem. All individual nonnegative differences therefore vanish, proving every surjection is an isomorphism. Rankzero gives the singleton unit lattice; the levelzero positive-rank quotient is zero. Homogeneity of generators and relations supplies the integer grading. This is the complete applicable BK2008 Theorems6.1/6.4 proof route, without inferring an individual block dimension directly from total dimension alone. No choice.

items.title: Degree and codegree of standard tableaux
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and a standard $\mu$-tableau
$T$, the addable and removable nodes of partitions, the symmetric form of the
cyclic affine type-$A$ Cartan datum, and the degree recursion of the graded
Specht definition.

[F1] Addable and removable nodes of a partition are as declared in
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]; node positions are
compared in the English diagram, with strictly above/below meaning in an
earlier/later row of the same component.

[F2] The degree $d_A(\mu)$ and the degree recursion
$\deg(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

[F3] The root form has $(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)=a_{ij}$, and the level-one weight pairs by $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i0}$. These are the required symmetric-form conventions for [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]; the root lattice and its positive cone are those of [[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]].

[F4] The weak Bruhat arrows $\to_T$ and the notion of a horizontal brick are
those of [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Counting addable and removable nodes (1).** Deleting the removable node $A$ of residue $i$ makes $A$ addable. Apart from this change, all corner changes occur immediately next to $A$ and have residues $i-1$ or $i+1$, which differ from $i$ since $e\ge2$ (for $e=2$ the two neighbor residues coincide with each other). Hence the signed count of $i$-nodes strictly above $A$ is unchanged, as is the signed count strictly below it. There is no other addable or removable $i$-node in the row of $A$. Splitting the signed corner count of $\mu$ into its above and below parts and the removable node $A$ therefore gives $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$. [F1, F2]

1.2 **The Cartan formula (2).** Write $u_j$ for the basis vector indexed by $j\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ in the free abelian group on residues, and choose $R$ greater than the number of nonzero rows of $\mu$. Put $b_r=\mu_r-r$. The signed corner vector is $\sum_i d_i(\mu)u_i=u_{-R}+\sum_{r=1}^R(u_{b_r+1}-u_{b_r})$: adjacent row-boundary terms cancel precisely when the corresponding node is not a corner, and the tail term cancels the artificial bottom boundary. For the empty partition this telescopes to $u_0$, so $d_i(\varnothing)=\delta_{i,0}=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)$. Adding a node of residue $j$ moves one $b_r=j-1$ to $j$ and changes this vector by $u_{j+1}-2u_j+u_{j-1}$. Thus each $d_i$ changes by $-a_{ij}$, including the double neighbor contribution when $e=2$. The vector with coordinates $(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$ has the same initial value and the same change when $\alpha$ increases by $\alpha_j$. Induction on the number of nodes proves (2). [F1, F3]

1.3 **Bricks in the first row (5)(i).** All nodes carrying $m,\ldots,d$ lie consecutively in one row, by [F4] and standardness; since they are the largest entries, they form the rightmost segment of that row. At every addition in the codegree recursion for a brick in row one, there are no rows strictly above, so the increment is zero. Summing these increments proves $\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le m-1})$. [F1, F4]

2.1 **The defect recursion (3).** Expanding, $\operatorname{def}(\alpha)-\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)-((\alpha,\alpha)-(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha-\alpha_i))/2=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)-(\alpha,\alpha_i)+(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)/2=d_i(\mu)+1$ by (2) and $(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)=2$, which is the displayed recursion [F3]. [F3, step 1.2]

3.1 **Degree plus codegree (4).** For $d=0$ both definitions give $0=\operatorname{def}(0)$. For $d>0$ let $A$ be the node containing $d$ and $i=\operatorname{res}A$; by the induction hypothesis applied to $T_{\le d-1}$ and by step 2.1, $\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$, where the middle equality uses (1) [F2, F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **Full residue bricks (5)(ii).** Suppose the terminal brick has $e$ nodes in row $r$ and occupies columns $c+1,\ldots,c+e$. Put $\lambda=T_{\le m-1}$. If $r=1$, step 1.3 applies. If $r>1$, standardness implies that all nodes in rows above $r$ already occur in $\lambda$ and that $\lambda_{r-1}\ge c+e$: each entry above a brick node is smaller, and all entries outside the terminal brick are at most $m-1$. Immediately before each of the $e$ additions, row $r$ therefore has length strictly smaller than $\lambda_{r-1}$. The signed corner counts strictly above row $r$ stay fixed throughout these pre-addition shapes. Indeed, in the top $r-1$ rows each maximal plateau of equal row lengths contributes one addable node at the start of its first row and one removable node at the end of its last row, and the last such row remains removable because its length is greater than that of row $r$ before the addition. Thus the number of addable corners above the brick equals the number of removable corners above it. The brick residues $(c+1-r),\ldots,(c+e-r)$ run through $I$ once. Summing the codegree increment for these residues counts each of the fixed above addable corners once positively and each above removable corner once negatively, giving zero. Hence the codegrees before and after the brick agree. The boundary count, defect recursion and tableau induction establish all five clauses by finite computations and use no choice. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.3] ∎

items.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
items.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an
equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends
finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift
$M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely
generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded
simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings
$\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. The inverse equivalence, restriction along $\rho^{-1}$, therefore
induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and
$G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and
the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed grading-preserving anti-involutions $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$
(i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor
intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective
Hom-dualities $\#$ of `def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals`,
and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual
indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block
isomorphism $\rho_\alpha$. DEFINE the Hecke duality by
$\ast_H=\rho_\alpha\ast_R\rho_\alpha^{-1}$. This is a grading-preserving
anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of $e(i),y_r,\psi_r$, and $\rho_\alpha$
intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies
blockwise. This does not identify $\ast_H$ with the raw cellular
anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a
product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An isomorphism $\rho:R\to H$ of finite-dimensional unital
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras, possibly intertwining fixed grading-preserving anti-involutions
$\ast_R$, $\ast_H$.

[F1] The graded module categories, the internal shift $M\{r\}$, finite
generated graded projectives and the Grothendieck and Cartan data are those of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]],
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] and
[[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]].

[F2] The graded Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$,
its additivity, sesquilinearity and degree-zero part are those of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]].

[F3] The Hecke-side grading and the block isomorphisms are supplied by
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading` and
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism`; the diagram dualities
are those of `def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals`, and
the left cell module used in the application is the one of
[[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Restriction of scalars is an equivalence.** Pulling back a graded left $H$-module $M$ along $\rho$ gives a graded left $R$-module with the same underlying graded vector space and action $r\cdot m=\rho(r)m$, and pulling back along $\rho^{-1}$ is a functor in the other direction; the two composites are the identity on underlying graded vector spaces and hence on objects and morphisms [F1]. Because $\rho$ is a bijection and preserves degree, the functor is exact, preserves finite-dimensionality, and satisfies $\rho^*M\{r\}=(\rho^*M)\{r\}$ [F1]. [F1]

1.2 **Projectives, Hom and composition multiplicities.** A finitely generated graded projective is a direct summand of a finite free graded module; pulling back preserves finite free modules and retracts, so it preserves finitely generated graded projectives [F1]. It is the identity on graded Hom spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{R,d}(P,\rho^*M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{H,d}(\rho_*P,M)$ and on shifts, so it preserves graded Hom dimensions and consequently composition multiplicities of graded simples together with their shifts; the graded Hom pairing of [F2] is therefore identified [F2]. [F1, F2]

2.1 **The Grothendieck identifications.** Since both inverse functors are exact and preserve split exact sequences, finite dimension and the shift, restriction along $\rho^{-1}$ induces $A$-linear isomorphisms $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R)\to K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R)\to G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H)$; the underlying module of a projective is carried to the underlying module, so the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$ are intertwined, and $q$ is preserved because shifts are [F1, F2]. [F1, F2, step 1.2]

2.2 **Dualities.** Suppose $\rho$ intertwines the stars. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$, the transported duality is $(a\cdot f)(m)=f(a^{\ast_H}m)$ on the dual space; substituting $a=\rho(x)$ and using $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$ shows that the duality computed with $\ast_R$ on $\rho^*M$ equals the duality computed with $\ast_H$ on $M$, so the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ are intertwined [F3]. The same substitution on $\operatorname{HOM}(P,R)\cong\operatorname{HOM}(\rho_*P,H)$ identifies the projective Hom-dualities $\#$; consequently normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives are preserved, since normalization is a shift-fixing condition [F3]. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **The application.** For each nonzero content sector the block isomorphism $\rho_\alpha$ is a graded algebra isomorphism [F3]. Defining $\ast_H=\rho_\alpha\ast_R\rho_\alpha^{-1}$ gives an anti-automorphism because a conjugation of an anti-automorphism is again one, it is an involution because $\ast_R$ is, it preserves the grading because $\rho_\alpha$ does, and it fixes the named images $\rho_\alpha(e(i)),\rho_\alpha(y_r),\rho_\alpha(\psi_r)$ whenever $\ast_R$ fixes the corresponding KLR generators; the intertwining $\rho_\alpha\ast_R=\ast_H\rho_\alpha$ holds by construction, so the duality conclusion of step 2.2 applies blockwise [F3]. No identification of $\ast_H$ with the raw cellular anti-involution is made, and no product-fixedness is inferred from fixedness of factors. [F3, step 2.2]

4.1 **No choice.** The construction is the inverse-pair of functors induced by an explicit bijection, and every verification is a one-line substitution on generators or Hom spaces; no family of nonempty sets is selected. Hence no choice is used. [F1, F3, given] ∎

items.title: The QG-8 categorification transports across the blockwise Hecke-KLR bridge
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers invoked below; the finite algebra transport introduces no additional choice.

In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] (both branches (C0)
and (CP)), fixing an admissible normalising series, the blockwise graded
isomorphism $\rho_\alpha:R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism` with the grading of
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading` transports the
standard homogeneous cyclotomic data to the Hecke side, block by block and then
by the restricted direct sums of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]:

1. the unique $A$-module isomorphism
$\phi:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda_0)$ of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module`
(sending the vacuum class to $v_{\Lambda_0}$ and intertwining the normalized
divided powers $E_i,F_i,K_i$) becomes an $A$-module isomorphism
$\phi^{\rm Hecke}:K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)$ with the same
properties;

2. the canonical identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}:G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$ of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module`
(restricted weight dual, canonical module action, normalized simple classes to
the form-dual projective basis) becomes an isomorphism
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$
with the same properties;

3. the two identifications intertwine the transported $E_i,F_i,K_i$ of
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero`
with the Hecke-side functors induced by
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and the
FIRST-BAR-SEQUILINEAR Hom pairing $h$ of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] and, separately,
the $A$-BILINEAR tensor pairing $T$ defining $\Psi_{\rm can}$, with
$h(P,M)=T(P^{\#},M)$. Both are weightwise perfect on normalized cover/simple
bases, where $P^{\#}=P$; they are not identified on arbitrary shifted first
arguments;

4. in branch (C0), and with the additional hypotheses of
`thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis`
and `thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis`
(symmetric Cartan datum with $d_i=1$, characteristic zero, finite loopless
quiver with arbitrary edge multiplicities and
$Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$), which the type-$A$
specialization of the regime satisfies, the transported normalized
$\#$self-dual indecomposable projectives correspond bijectively to the lower
global basis and the transported normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simples to the
upper global basis; the transported simple and projective crystals are the
$B(\Lambda_0)$-crystals of
`thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda`, so
each class carries its crystal label in $RP$.

In BOTH branches the normalized finite-module duality representatives and their
right crystal labels come from
`def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals` and
`thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda`,
independently of clause (4)'s characteristic-zero global-basis conclusion.

No based-quotient, quantum-star or cyclotomic categorification statement is
asserted beyond these transported clauses. Choice is inherited through the cited highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers.
