## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The nondegenerate level-one regime with its fixed admissible
normalising series, the blockwise graded isomorphisms $\rho_\alpha$, and the
standard homogeneous cyclotomic data on the KLR side.

[F1] The transport of the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups, its
Cartan maps, its forgetful maps, its graded Hom pairing and its diagram
dualities along a graded algebra isomorphism is the content of
[[lem-graded-algebra-isomorphism-transports-the-graded-module-category]].

[F2] The Hecke-side groups, Cartan map and pairing are the transported data of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] and
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]; the Hecke-side
induction and restriction functors are those of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]].

[F3] The type-$A$ specialization has $d_i=1$ and the finite loopless
cyclic quiver with arrows $i\to i+1$. For $e\ge3$, a forward adjacent pair
has $(h_{ij},h_{ji})=(1,0)$ and $Q^A_{ij}(u,v)=v-u$, while the reverse
pair has $(0,1)$ and $Q^A_{ji}(u,v)=u-v$; for $e=2$ both arrow
multiplicities are $1$ and $Q^A_{01}=Q^A_{10}=-(u-v)^2$. Nonadjacent
pairs have $Q^A_{ij}=1$. Thus in every case
$Q^A_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$
([[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]],
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]); the cyclotomic
quotient is the standard homogeneous one of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]].

[F4] The blockwise isomorphism, the grading, the finite-dimensionality and
symmetry of blocks are
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism`,
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading` and
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric`; the
KLR-side identifications, the functor action, the global bases and the crystal
correspondence are
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module`,
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module`,
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero`,
`thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis`,
`thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis` and
`thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda`.

[C1] Choice is inherited through the highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers of [F4];
the transport itself introduces none
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [F1]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Transport of the projective identification.** By [F1] the blockwise graded isomorphisms $\rho_\alpha$ induce an $A$-linear isomorphism $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)\to K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)$ which intertwines shifts, Cartan maps and forgetful maps, block by block and then on the restricted direct sums. Composing the inverse of this transport with the KLR-side isomorphism $\phi$ of [F4] gives $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$; the vacuum class is preserved because $\rho_\alpha$ is the identity on the underlying vector spaces and fixes the vacuum sector, and the divided powers are intertwined because the Hecke-side $E_i,F_i,K_i$ are defined to be the transported KLR functors [F1, F2, F4]. This proves (1). [F1, F2, F4]

1.2 **Transport of the module identification.** Applying the same transport to the exact functor on finite-dimensional graded modules gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)\to G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)$ preserving internal shifts, composition multiplicities and the diagram dualities, by [F1]. Composing the inverse of this transport with $\Psi_{\rm can}$ of [F4] gives $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ with the same restricted-weight-dual target, the same canonical module action transported through the functor, and normalized simple classes mapping to the form-dual projective basis; this proves (2). [F1, F2, F4]

1.3 **Functors and pairings.** The Hecke-side functors $E_i,F_i$ are by definition the images of the KLR functors under the blockwise equivalences, so the transported identifications intertwine them with the quantum action of [F4] [F1, F2]. The graded Hom pairing is identified by [F1], and the identity $h(P,M)=T(P^{\#},M)$ is the native comparison recorded in [F4] between the Hom pairing and the tensor pairing defining $\Psi_{\rm can}$; both are weightwise perfect on the normalized cover and simple bases because on those bases $P^{\#}=P$ and the actual unscaled cover/simple pairing clause of the module $G_0$ supplier makes the two pairings evaluate to the same delta, while the first-bar rule on shifts is retained on arbitrary shifted first arguments rather than identified with the bilinear form [F1, F2, F4]. This proves (3). [F1, F2, F4]

1.4 **Clause (4) and the type-A hypothesis check.** By [F3] the type-$A$ specialization has $d_i=1$, a symmetric Cartan matrix and the finite loopless cyclic quiver; for $e\ge3$ the ordered adjacent multiplicities are $(1,0)$ or $(0,1)$ and for $e=2$ they are $(1,1)$, giving exactly $Q^A_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ in both cases. Branch (C0) supplies characteristic zero, so all geometric-parameter hypotheses of the two global-basis theorems hold; transporting their conclusions along the blockwise equivalences identifies the normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives with the lower global basis and the normalized self-dual simples with the upper global basis [F1, F3, F4]. Since the transported functor preserves shifts and dualities, the crystals are the $B(\Lambda_0)$-crystals of [F4] and each class carries its label in the restricted set $RP$ [F3, F4]. [F1, F3, F4]

2.1 **Both branches and Choice.** In an arbitrary branch of the regime the normalized finite-module duality representatives and their right crystal labels exist by the duality and crystal suppliers of [F4] alone, so clauses (1)-(3) hold in both branches and clause (4) only adds the characteristic-zero global-basis correspondence [F4]. No new choice is made: [C1] is inherited through the global-basis suppliers, and all transport verifications are finite substitutions. [C1, F1, F4, given] ∎

items.title: Shifted degrees and Garnir exchanges for standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and $r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the Cartan matrix of the regime.
2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition, then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$ in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].
3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and $S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.
items.strategy: 1 is [BKW, Proposition 3.13]: reduce to $r=d-1$ and compare the two expressions for $\deg(T)$ and $\deg(S)$; the difference is $d_B(\mu^A)-d_B(\mu)$ for the nodes $A$ (containing $d$) and $B$ (containing $d-1$), and the four residue cases (equal residues, adjacent single edge, the $e=2$ double edge, and non-adjacent) give exactly $-2,1,2,0=-a_{i_{d-1}i_d}$. 2 is [BKW, Corollary 3.14], obtained from 1 by multiplying the adjacent transpositions of the reduced word and adding the degrees $\deg(\psi_re(i_T))$. 3 is [BKW, Proposition 3.16]: using the tableau-order Lemma 3.9 reduce to a two-row Garnir belt; the exchange condition $i_S=i_{s_rT}$ splits the belt into bricks of size divisible by $e$ plus at most one exceptional brick per row; Lemma 3.15 computes $\operatorname{codeg}(S)$ and $\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ by the congruence classes of $b$ modulo $e$, and the difference is $-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ in each case. All steps are finite residue and brick computations; no choice. For the strict Garnir case retain the maximal standard belt tableau and strict Bruhat lower condition. Reduce to a two-row belt ending at its final node by the agreement-outside-belt lemma. Remove complete horizontal e-bricks using the ABOVE codegree lemma. The lower tableau has residual codegree -1 if b is nonzero modulo e and 0 otherwise. The Garnir tableau has codegree0/1 for e>2, and1/2 for e=2, respectively. Their difference gives degree1/2 in the single/double-edge cases. Equal-color degree in a standard exchange remains -2, from the Cartan diagonal; it is not assigned +2.

items.title: The graded Specht module has a homogeneous tableau basis
items.statement:
Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with $a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of $S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].
2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced decompositions of the same $w_T$, then $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\unlhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$; in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is independent of the choices.
3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ are homogeneous, with $$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$ Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis $\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).
items.strategy: Follow [BKW, §4.2-4.3]: (1) expand $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu$ in the standard basis using the quadratic relation, the dot-sliding relations and Lemma 4.1 ($y_rz_\mu=0$, $X_rz_\mu=\xi^{i_r}z_\mu$), and use Proposition 4.3 (triangularity of the $z$-basis) to identify the leading coefficient, which is nonzero exactly for standard $T$. (2) By Matsumoto's theorem it suffices to compare two words differing by one braid relation; the quadratic/braid relations express the difference as a combination of shorter words with the stated weight and degree, and induction on length plus (1) gives the claim. (3) Compute $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ by moving the generators through the reduced word using the mixed relations; every occurring vector has weight $i_T$ or $i_{s_rT}$ and the degrees follow from [[prop-shifted-degrees-and-garnir-exchanges-for-standard-tableaux]] (1) and the definition of $\deg(T)$; the codegree identities of [[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]] supply the bookkeeping in the terminal/Garnir cases. The $q$-character formula is then immediate from the homogeneous basis, and forgetting the grading gives the ungraded cell module by construction. This is [BKW, Theorem 4.10] restated; the independence statement is its part (i). No choice.

items.axiom_use: None: finite integer PBW, crossing straightening, finite rational kernels and the choice-free regular-trace/finite-root-field head helper.
items.statement:
Fix the level-one type-A integer KLR presentation, charge $0$, and finite quantum characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\ldots\}$. Let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field in the specified Hecke regime, let $\lambda$ be the specified partition, and let $S_K(\lambda)$ be the LEFT graded Murphy cell Specht module with its specified initial cyclic generator $z_K$. Then there is a finite-dimensional graded module $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ for the rational KLR algebra, with a specified homogeneous cyclic vector $z_{\mathbb Q}$, and a graded generator-preserving isomorphism $K\otimes_{\mathbb Q} S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)\cong S_K(\lambda)$. The rational module is explicitly presented by the initial weight, dot and horizontal crossing relations, together with one homogeneous rational relation for each Garnir belt. Each of these relations is the unique vector with Garnir coefficient $1$ in the kernel of a finite matrix with integer entries, obtained from crossing operators in the integer row permutation module. It therefore depends only on the integer presentation, not on a choice of $K$ or of a root of unity.

If the specified normalized simple head $D_K(\lambda)$ is nonzero and absolutely simple, this construction, combined with the local cyclic-head descent lemma, defines its initial-generator image line over $\mathbb Q$ up to scalar. The orbit of that image under the finite integer cyclotomic algebra is a lattice of rank $\dim_K D_K(\lambda)$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] gives the affine KLR PBW basis. Dot slides remove one crossing from correction terms, quadratic moves remove two, and three-term braid corrections remove three. Preferred reduced expressions differ by terms with strictly fewer crossings.

[F2] [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] fixes the integer coefficients and the source BK/BKW crossing convention $\psi=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$. This proof uses that convention directly; it does not identify KMR's reversed-orientation crossing with it.

[F3] [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] supplies the LEFT Murphy cell Specht module's homogeneous standard basis $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_K$ and triangularity: for every tableau $T$, $v_T$ is a combination of standard $v_U$ with $w_U\le w_T$ in strong Bruhat order. Idempotents and grading restrict this expansion to the vector's weight and degree.

[F4] The specified initial vector has weight $i^\lambda$, all dots kill it, and a crossing kills it when its two successive entries occupy the same initial row. These are the initial-generator relations in the reviewed BKW construction, not conditions imposed on an arbitrary vector in a simple.

[F5] [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] proves characteristic-zero radical base change by the regular trace pairing, hence descends a rational cyclic module's normalized simple head and its specified generator image, and proves the lattice rank.

[F6] [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]] gives the finite free integer cyclotomic algebra used in step 5.2. The local PBW straightening used before that quotient is integral: its monic moves have integer coefficients, and independence follows by rational scalar extension of the supplied PBW basis.

## Proof

**Given:** The stated level-one integer presentation, the specified LEFT cell module and its initial generator, and F1–F5. No Axiom of Choice is used.

1.1 Put $\kappa=0$ in the residue formulas below. Work first in the affine content algebra $R_{\mathbb Z}$ before the cyclotomic quotient. For each row of $\lambda$, the successive residue segment has a one-dimensional integral module on which its word idempotent is $1$ and its dots and internal crossings are $0$. The KLR relations hold: successive colours are distinct, their quadratic at zero dots is $0$, and a possible three-strand repeated-endpoint pattern occurs only for $e=2$, where its double-edge braid correction also vanishes at zero dots. Induce the tensor product of these segment modules, and shift its generator $m_0$ to degree $\deg(T_0)$, where $T_0$ is row reading. Denote the result by $M_{\mathbb Z}$. [F2, construct, algebra]

1.2 Let $P$ be the Young row subgroup. Choose reduced expressions compatible with the unique decomposition $w=d p$, with $d$ a minimal representative for $S_d/P$ and $p\in P$, and $\ell(w)=\ell(d)+\ell(p)$. F1 then makes the inducing bimodule free over the row algebra on the minimal-representative words. Tensoring the one-dimensional row modules shows that $M_{\mathbb Z}$ has the integral basis $m_T=\psi_{w_T}m_0$ indexed by all row-strict tableaux $T$. Its cyclic presentation is exactly the initial weight, dot and horizontal-crossing relations. In particular all generator-action matrices on this finite basis have integer entries. Put $M_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes M_{\mathbb Z}$; scalar extension gives $M_K=K\otimes M_{\mathbb Q}$. By F4, there is a surjective graded map $\pi_K:M_K\to S_K(\lambda)$ carrying $m_0$ exactly to $z_K$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 Crossing straightening gives a filtration useful below: a word with at most $N$ crossings applied to $m_0$ is a combination of $m_U$ with $\ell(w_U)\le N$. Move dots right, reduce nonreduced words by quadratic and Coxeter moves, compare reduced words, and split off the right row subgroup as in step 1.2. Positive dot powers kill $m_0$; a nontrivial row factor ends in an internal crossing and also kills $m_0$. Every correction has fewer crossings. In particular if $s_rT$ is row-strict and $\ell(w_{s_rT})=\ell(w_T)+1$, then $\psi_r m_T=m_{s_rT}$ plus terms of strictly smaller crossing length, with leading coefficient exactly $1$. If $s_rT$ is not row-strict, its possible leading term is killed by the right row factor and only shorter terms remain. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Fix a Garnir node $A=(a,b)$ with $(a+1,b)\in\lambda$. Its belt consists of the row-$a$ suffix $X$ beginning at column $b$ and row-$(a+1)$ prefix $Y$ ending at column $b$. The entries in these nodes in $T_0$ form one consecutive interval $J=\{u,\ldots,v\}$: the suffix ends at the last position of row $a$, immediately followed by the prefix at the beginning of row $a+1$. Let $G_A$ agree with $T_0$ outside the belt and fill $Y$ first, then $X$, increasingly with $J$. It is row-strict and nonstandard. This $G_A$ is the nonstandard belt filling used for the rational-kernel presentation; it is distinct from the maximal STANDARD Garnir tableau in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]. [construct, algebra]

2.2 Among ALL row-strict tableaux agreeing with $T_0$ outside this belt, $G_A$ is the only nonstandard one. For columns $c<b$, the upper entry is an unchanged number less than $u$, hence less than every changed lower entry. For columns $c>b$, the lower entry, if present, is unchanged and greater than $v$, hence greater than every changed upper entry. Comparisons with the row above or the row below have the same strict bounds, and every other column comparison is unchanged. Thus only column $b$ can fail. It fails precisely when the first upper-belt entry exceeds the last lower-belt entry. Since each of the two rows is increasing, this is equivalent to every upper-belt entry exceeding every lower-belt entry, and hence to the unique filling $G_A$. [step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 On $J$, the residue word $i(G_A)$ is one successive-residue segment. Along $Y$ the residues increase by $1$; its final node $(a+1,b)$ has residue $\kappa+b-a-1$. The first node of $X$, $(a,b)$, has residue $\kappa+b-a$, and the rest again increase by $1$. Consequently $i(G_A)_r\ne i(G_A)_{r+1}$ for every $u\le r<v$, including $e=2$. This distinctness, rather than any braid normalization, is essential. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

2.4 Let $\delta_A=\deg(\psi_{w_{G_A}}e(i^\lambda))+\deg(T_0)$ and let $T_A^{\mathbb Q}$ be the span of those integral basis vectors $m_T$ for which $T$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt, has weight $i(G_A)$, and has homogeneous degree $\delta_A$. It includes $m_{G_A}$. The use of the entire weight-degree slice avoids any brick-classification assumption. Write $T_A^K=K\otimes T_A^{\mathbb Q}$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct]

2.5 The vector $\pi_K(m_{G_A})$ is a combination of images of standard basis vectors in $T_A^K$. Indeed F3 gives standard $U$ with $w_U\le w_{G_A}$. The permutation $w_{G_A}$ belongs to the parabolic subgroup generated by $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$, since it permutes only $J$. Every Bruhat-smaller permutation belongs to this same subgroup: choose a reduced word for $w_{G_A}$ in these generators, and use the defining subword characterization of strong Bruhat order. Hence $U$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt. Weight idempotents discard different words, and homogeneity discards different degrees, leaving exactly the standard vectors in the slice of step 2.4. By step 2.2, every other vector of the slice is standard; by F3 its image is part of the standard Specht basis and is linearly independent. Therefore $\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$ is precisely one-dimensional, including the case where the image of $m_{G_A}$ is zero. [F3, step 2.2, step 2.4, algebra]

3.1 For every $u\le r<v$, the image $\psi_r T_A^K$ in $M_K$ is spanned by standard row-strict belt tableaux. To see the support assertion, choose reduced words for all belt permutations using only $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$. Straightening a crossing supported in this interval never introduces a crossing outside it; factoring a right row permutation also uses only this interval. Thus every resulting row-strict basis tableau agrees outside the belt. The image has fixed weight $s_r i(G_A)$, which differs from $i(G_A)$ by step 2.3. Its support cannot include the sole nonstandard belt tableau $G_A$. Hence the entire image has standard support by step 2.2, and $\pi_K$ is injective on its span by F3. [F1, F3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, algebra]

3.2 If $x\in\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$, then $\pi_K(\psi_r x)=\psi_r\pi_K(x)=0$. The injectivity in step 3.1 implies $\psi_r x=0$ in $M_K$ for every inside-belt crossing. Thus this one-dimensional Specht-kernel line lies in $B_A^K:=\bigcap_{r=u}^{v-1}\ker(\psi_r:T_A^K\to M_K)$. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]

3.3 The $m_{G_A}$ coefficient map is injective on $B_A^K$. Suppose a nonzero $x\in B_A^K$ has that coefficient zero. Choose a tableau $T$ with nonzero coefficient in $x$ whose crossing length $N=\ell(w_T)$ is maximal. It is standard by step 2.2. Record membership in $X$ or $Y$ for the successive numbers $u,\ldots,v$ as a binary word. Unless this word is all $Y$ then all $X$, it has an adjacent occurrence $XY$; that excluded word is exactly $G_A$. Choose such an occurrence at $r,r+1$. Swapping them preserves row strictness because they lie in different rows and are consecutive numbers; it increases permutation length by $1$, because $r$ is in the earlier row. Its weight becomes $s_r i(G_A)\ne i(G_A)$, so it cannot be $G_A$ and is also standard by step 2.2. By step 1.3, the coefficient of $m_{s_rT}$ in $\psi_r x$ at length $N+1$ is precisely the nonzero coefficient of $m_T$ in $x$. A lower-length input cannot reach length $N+1$; a different equal-length input has a different possible leading tableau because $s_r$ is injective; and its correction terms have smaller length. Therefore $\psi_r x\ne0$, contradicting $x\in B_A^K$. [step 1.3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.2, algebra]

3.4 Consequently $\dim_K B_A^K\le1$, while step 3.2 gives a nonzero line inside it. Thus $B_A^K=\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$. Define $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ using the same intersection of crossing kernels over $\mathbb Q$. These are kernels of a single finite stacked matrix with integer entries on the explicitly selected integral row-strict bases. Row reduction over $\mathbb Q$ commutes with extension to $K$, so $B_A^K=K\otimes B_A^{\mathbb Q}$. It follows that $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ is one-dimensional and has a unique rational vector $h_A$ with coefficient $1$ on $m_{G_A}$. Its scalar extension is exactly the Specht-kernel vector with that normalization. This is an explicit rational linear-system construction of the relation, not an assumption that a chosen vector belongs to a rational form. [step 1.2, step 3.2, step 3.3, algebra]

4.1 Every other row-strict belt tableau has strictly smaller crossing length than $G_A$. Outside the belt there are no inversions involving belt entries because the belt interval is consecutive in row reading and its values form $J$. Inside, inversions are exactly upper/lower pairs with the upper entry larger. The tableau $G_A$ has all $|X||Y|$ such inversions, whereas every other filling loses at least one. Hence $h_A=m_{G_A}+\sum_{U:\,\ell(w_U)<\ell(w_{G_A})}c_U m_U$ with rational $c_U$, and it is homogeneous of degree $\delta_A$ by its definition in the slice. [step 2.1, step 2.4, step 3.4, algebra]

4.2 Put $S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}=M_{\mathbb Q}/\sum_A R_{\mathbb Q}h_A$. We prove standard spanning locally. For any nonstandard row-strict $T$, choose a vertical inversion at $(a,b),(a+1,b)$. All entries in its upper suffix $X$ exceed all entries in its lower prefix $Y$. Its Garnir factor $G_A$ therefore satisfies $T=wG_A$ with $w=w_Tw_{G_A}^{-1}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(w_T)-\ell(w_{G_A})$: reordering the contiguous belt's one-line list from $X,Y$ to $Y,X$ removes precisely its $|X||Y|$ cross inversions, while preserving within-part and outside comparisons. Reduced-word straightening and the relation $h_A=0$ replace $m_T$ by words with fewer than $\ell(w_T)$ crossings, by step 4.1. The filtration of step 1.3 expresses these as row-strict vectors of strictly smaller length. Induction proves that standard vectors span the quotient. [F1, step 1.3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

4.3 Scalar extension of the rational quotient presentation gives $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}=K\otimes S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}$. Every $h_A$ lies in $\ker\pi_K$ by step 3.4, so $\pi_K$ induces a surjection $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}\to S_K(\lambda)$ preserving the generator and grading. The source is spanned by the standard vectors by step 4.2, and their images are the linearly independent standard Specht basis by F3. Hence this map is an isomorphism. In particular the rational module is finite-dimensional, has its standard basis, and its generator maps exactly to $z_K$. [F3, step 3.4, step 4.2, algebra]

5.1 The rational module factors through the cyclotomic quotient. Each specified cyclotomic relation acts as zero after extension to $K$, because the module in step 4.3 is the specified cyclotomic Hecke cell Specht module. The matrix of that action on the rational standard basis has rational entries; faithful field extension forces it to be zero already over $\mathbb Q$. Denote this rational cyclotomic module by $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$, with generator $z_{\mathbb Q}$ the class of $m_0$. This identifies the required rational initial cyclic generator, not merely the unpointed module's isomorphism class. [step 4.3, algebra]

5.2 If an integer cyclic quotient is desired for F5, take the saturated generator annihilator $I_{\mathbb Z}=\{a\in A_{\mathbb Z}:a z_{\mathbb Q}=0\}$ in the finite integer cyclotomic algebra of [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]]. It is a homogeneous left ideal, and $A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ identifies with the integral orbit $A_{\mathbb Z}z_{\mathbb Q}\subset S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$. Its rational span is the entire rational module by cyclicity, so $\mathbb Q\otimes(A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z})\cong S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ with the specified generator. Clearing denominators in each $h_A$ is also possible, but no unsaturated integer quotient or integral Specht-freeness theorem is needed. [step 5.1, algebra]

5.3 Apply F5 to this pointed rational form and the supplied absolutely simple normalized head. Its radical-basechange proof gives a rational normalized head with the image of $z_{\mathbb Q}$; absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed head differ only by a scalar. Its integral-algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free, with rational span that head, so its rank is exactly the head's $K$-dimension. This establishes the precise requested initial-generator line and lattice statement over arbitrary characteristic-zero $K$. No three-brick identity, unproved R-matrix formula, arbitrary-vector rational form, or change of the specified generator enters the argument. [F5, step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Graded Specht restriction has the removable-node filtration
items.statement:
Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], let $\mu$ be a partition of $d$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $i\in I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. Let $A_1,\dots,A_c$ be the removable $i$-nodes of $\mu$ ordered from bottom to top, and let $\mu^{A_m}=\mu\setminus A_m$. Write $E_i:=E_i^{\rm basic}$ for the restriction functor $N\mapsto e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)N$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] (equivalently the $i$-part of the tower restriction of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]). Then $E_iS(\mu)$ has a filtration $$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_c=E_iS(\mu)$$ of graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-modules with $V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})\{d_{A_m}(\mu)\}$ for $1\le m\le c$.

Equivalently, the restriction of $S(\mu)$ to the previous rank has the removable-node filtration of [BKW, Theorem 4.11] over ALL removable nodes, and $E_i$ selects the removable-$i$-node part. No choice is used.
items.strategy: By [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] the module $S(\mu)$ has the homogeneous tableau basis $\{v_T\}$ with $v_T\in e(i_T)S(\mu)$, so the idempotent projection $e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)S(\mu)$ is spanned by those $v_T$ whose last letter is $i$, i.e. whose maximal entry $d$ occupies a removable $i$-node. items.title: Graded Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
items.statement: In the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], let $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$ be the transported identification of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]], and let $S_\mu:=\pi(M_\mu)$ be the standard monomial image of the standard Fock vector $M_\mu$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]] under the projection to the basic module. Then for every partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$, $$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}\bigl([S(\mu)]\bigr)=S_\mu .$$ In other words, the class of the graded Specht module of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] is the standard Fock vector in the fixed level-one convention. This holds in both branches (C0) and (CP). No choice beyond the inherited suppliers is used.
items.strategy: Use the canonical native11 normalization throughout, not the KK map. At content beta let h_i(beta)=<h_i,Lambda0-beta>. The actual removable-node filtration computes BASIC restriction as sum_A q^{d_A(mu)}[S(mu minus A)]. Canonical E_i is q^{-1-h_i(beta)} times that restriction. For a removable i-node A the omitted removable A gives d_A(mu)+d^A(mu)=h_i(beta)+1, where d^A counts addable-minus-removable i-nodes strictly ABOVE A. Thus E_can[S(mu)]=sum_A q^{-d^A(mu)}[S(mu minus A)]. The symmetric linear-J Fock model and its field orthogonal projection supplied by the declared quantum9/23 interfaces satisfy precisely E_i pi(M_mu)=sum_A q^{-d^A(mu)}pi(M_(mu minus A)). Induct from the vacuum. The canonical transported map intertwines E_can, so all E_i kill the difference at positive root degree. Inside the irreducible Q(q) highest-weight module a nonzero vector killed by every E_i generates a highest-weight submodule; at a lower weight it cannot contain the original highest vector, contradicting irreducibility. Therefore the difference vanishes. Torsion-freeness of the restricted integral dual makes this equality valid over A. The argument uses only the declared current symmetric-model canonical recursion, never the source's bare-restriction recursion under a different normalization. It works in both field branches; q is independent of the Hecke parameter. No new choice.

items.title: Ariki's canonical basis theorem in characteristic zero
items.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the normalized
self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$ and their normalized projective covers
$Y(\lambda)$ labelled by the crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$ as in
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4):

1. the transported isomorphism
$\phi^{\rm Hecke}:K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)$ sends the class
of the normalized self-dual indecomposable projective $Y(\lambda)$ to the lower
global basis vector $G(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda\in RP$;

2. the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$
sends $[D(\lambda)]$ to the upper global basis vector $G^*(\lambda)$, form-dual
to $G(\lambda)$ under the highest-weight contravariant form;

3. equivalently the lower global basis is the canonical basis of the basic
module $V_A(\Lambda_0)$ and corresponds to projective indecomposables, while
the upper global basis is the dual-canonical basis and corresponds to simple
classes, and the labels are those of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4): the
crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$, with a simple and its projective cover carrying the
same label. The passage from these crystal labels to the
cellular/Dipper--James parametrization of the simple modules is not asserted
here; it is established with the head classification later on this page;

4. specializing the grading $q=1$ via the forgetful maps $\zeta$ of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]
recovers Ariki's ungraded canonical-basis statement, and combined with the
graded decomposition theorem later on this page it gives his ungraded
decomposition-number theorem.

Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers; no choice is
introduced by the transport or by the label comparison.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Branch (C0) of the nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized
self-dual simples and projective covers, and the transported identifications.

[F1] The QG-8 transport identifies the KLR-side canonical data with the
Hecke-side groups: clause (1) transports $\phi$ to $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$, clause
(2) transports $\Psi_{\rm can}$ to $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$, and clause (4)
identifies the transported normalized self-dual projectives with the lower
global basis, the transported normalized self-dual simples with the upper
global basis, and the transported crystals with the $B(\Lambda_0)$-crystals
labelled in $RP$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

[F2] The lower and upper global bases, their duality
$B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$ under the contravariant
form, and their crystal compatibility are those of
[[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]],
[[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] and
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; the KLR
side conclusions are
`thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis`
and `thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis`.

[F3] The transport of the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups, its
Cartan and forgetful maps and its dualities along the blockwise graded
isomorphism is the content of
[[lem-graded-algebra-isomorphism-transports-the-graded-module-category]]; the
forgetful maps satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

[F4] The Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]), with the
restricted coordinate functionals and the transition polynomials of
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]] and
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]].

[C1] Choice is inherited through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Projectives to the lower basis (1).** By [F1] the transported isomorphism $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$ is the QG-8 transport of the KLR-side identification, under which the normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives correspond bijectively to the lower global basis; the transport preserves the classes of the underlying modules and internal shifts, so the class of $Y(\lambda)$ is sent to $G(\lambda)$ for every restricted label $\lambda$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2]

1.2 **Simples to the upper basis (2).** The same clause identifies the transported normalized self-dual simples with the upper global basis, and the upper family is form-dual to the lower family under the contravariant form by [F2]; hence $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([D(\lambda)])=G^*(\lambda)$ with $B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2]

1.3 **Labels and non-assertion (3).** On the KLR side the crystals are constructed from the one-step socle and head operators and identified with $B(\Lambda_0)$; the transport preserves the crystal structure, so each transported class carries its intrinsic label in $RP$ and no permutation of labels is left open [F1]. The identification of these crystal labels with the cellular or Dipper--James head labels is deliberately not asserted here; only the transported identifications of clauses (1) and (2) are claimed [F1, F4]. [F1, F4]

1.4 **The ungraded specialization (4).** The forgetful maps satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$ and specialize $q$ to $1$ [F3]; a graded composition series of a finite-dimensional graded module specializes to an ungraded composition series with the same multiplicities, and the transported identifications therefore specialize to the ungraded statement that the self-dual projective classes are the canonical basis and the simple classes the dual-canonical basis of the basic module, which is Ariki's ungraded canonical-basis statement [F1, F3]. Combining this specialization with the graded decomposition theorem of this page gives the ungraded decomposition-number statement; that combination is recorded as the pointer in clause (4) and is not used in the present proofs [F3, F4]. [F1, F3, F4]

2.1 **Choice.** The transport functor, the label comparison and the specialization are explicit finite constructions on finite-dimensional blocks; the only choice is inherited through the global-basis suppliers, as recorded in [C1]. [C1, F1, given] ∎

items.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
items.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition
$\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded
composition multiplicity satisfies
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$
where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in
$G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless
$\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded
decomposition-number theorem
$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the
QG-8 global-basis suppliers.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Branch (C0) of the regime, a partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$,
the graded Specht module $S(\mu)$, and the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$.

[F1] The transported identification sends $[S(\mu)]$ to the standard Fock
vector $S_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)$
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]); and
$S_\mu=\sum_\lambda d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ over the restricted
labels, with the same coefficients as the lower expansion, by
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]].

[F2] In branch (C0) the transported normalized self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$
map to the upper global basis vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ under
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2)), and the
simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$
([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)).

[F3] The transition polynomials have off-diagonal entries in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ and are supported
on $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ with diagonal $1$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]);
the graded module group is the restricted direct sum of the blockwise groups
with forgetful maps $\zeta$ satisfying $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

[F4] The graded Specht module and its basis are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the regime is
branch (C0) of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]].

[C1] Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis and Fock suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Transport the Specht class.** Applying $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ to $[S(\mu)]$ gives $S_\mu$ by [F1], and the expansion of the standard vector in the upper family is $S_\mu=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ by [F1]; the coefficients are the transition polynomials of [F3]. [F1, F3]

2.1 **Replace the upper basis by the simple classes.** By [F2] the vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ are the images of the simple classes $[D(\lambda)]$ under the same isomorphism; applying $(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}$ to step 1.1 therefore gives the expansion $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 **Read off multiplicities and support.** Since the simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ by [F2], the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in the expansion of step 2.1 is the graded composition multiplicity $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$, and it equals $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)$; the support statement $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ is the triangularity of [F3]. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 **The ungraded specialization.** The forgetful map $\zeta$ specializes $q$ to $1$ and sends a graded composition series to an ungraded one with the same multiplicities [F3]; applying $\zeta$ to the expansion of step 2.1 gives $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(1)$, Ariki's ungraded decomposition-number theorem. No new choice is made: [C1] is inherited. [C1, F3, F4, given] ∎

items.title: Graded Specht heads classify the graded simple modules
items.statement:
In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for
$\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ the graded Specht module $S(\lambda)$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] has irreducible
head, denoted $\dot D(\lambda)$, and
$\dot D(\lambda)^\circledast\cong\dot D(\lambda)$. Moreover:

1. the modules $\{\dot D(\lambda)\langle m\rangle:\lambda\in RP_\alpha,\ m\in\mathbb Z\}$
are a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic graded simple
$R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules (equivalently, of $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ with the
transported grading);

2. in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ one has
$[S(\lambda)]=[\dot D(\lambda)]+(\ast)$ if $\lambda$ is restricted and
$[S(\lambda)]=(\ast)$ otherwise, where $(\ast)$ is an $A$-linear combination of
$[\dot D(\mu)]$'s with $\mu\lhd\lambda$; consequently
$[S(\mu):\dot D(\lambda)]_q\ne0$ implies $\lambda\unlhd\mu$, and
$[S(\lambda):\dot D(\lambda)]_q=1$;

3. in branch (C0), $\dot D(\lambda)\cong D(\lambda)$, the normalized simple
with crystal label $\lambda$ of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4);
separately, after forgetting the grading and converting the ordinary right
modules through star, $\dot D(\lambda)\cong(D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'})^{\theta}$ by
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`. Thus the
conjugate $e$-regular ordinary label occurs with the explicit
sign-automorphism pullback, which reflects residue content and is not an
untwisted same-block identification. The ordinary module dictionary and radical
comparison hold in both field branches; the crystal-label comparison in this
part is the stated (C0) assertion.

Parts (1) and (2) hold in both branches (C0) and (CP); part (3) is stated in
branch (C0), the branch of the decomposition theorem it consumes. The branch
(CP) analogue of (3) is the identification [BK 2009, Theorem 5.18] and is NOT
asserted here. Choice is inherited only through the cited transported
global-basis suppliers, as recorded in the contract.
items.strategy: Apply the actual finite-cell classification of nonzero-form heads and factor ordering. Invert the restricted unitriangular transition minor to express an unrestricted Specht class in strictly dominated restricted Specht classes; cellular factor ordering excludes a nonzero-form head at that unrestricted label. All distinguished labels are thus restricted, and comparing the simple-class Grothendieck rank with the restricted Specht basis count proves every restricted label is distinguished. The local cellular diagonal and smaller-factor clauses supply the head expansion. In C0 compare the crystal-labelled and head-labelled unitriangular expansions by finite dominance induction. Use finite duality and the leading coefficient to fix the zero duality shift, and independently retain the actual signed-conjugate ordinary Specht/form dictionary across both branches. No new Choice is introduced.

items.title: Reduction of characteristic-zero simple modules modulo p
items.strategy: Apply [[lem-rational-garnir-annihilator-lines-present-the-specified-specht-generator]] to the specified LEFT Murphy cell module and its initial homogeneous cyclic generator. Its finite integral row-permutation crossing matrices define a rational simultaneous Garnir-annihilator line; the strict crossing filtration proves standard spanning, and the actual homogeneous standard basis proves generator-preserving scalar-extension equality. It factors through the finite integer cyclotomic algebra by faithful rational scalar extension. Then [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] identifies the radical by the regular trace pairing, proves rational radical base change, and descends the specified simple head and initial-generator image. Absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed normalized head differ only by a scalar. Thus the special vector lies in a scalar multiple of this proved rational form. No arbitrary-vector rational descent, KMR brick identity, or ordinary DJ comparison is used in this lattice step. The integer algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free by the integral algebra theorem, spans the rational head by cyclicity, and is homogeneous; hence it is a full lattice of rank equal to the K-dimension. Word idempotents give graded direct summands, whose ranks survive tensoring with F, proving equality of graded word characters. Any other full homogeneous stable lattice has those same word-component ranks; the actual extremal-word character lemma proves G0 injectivity, so its reduction has the same G0 class. No assertion that all arbitrary K-lattices are literally commensurable without a rational/scalar identification is needed. Finally the restricted Specht classes are an A-basis of the UPPER dual lattice, have field-independent characters, and map under the corrected canonical identification to the same pi(M_mu). Character injectivity therefore shows that modules of equal characters over the two fields have equal images under Psi_can. Apply this to J(lambda) and the normalized characteristic-zero simple and invoke the characteristic-zero upper-basis theorem, proving part(3). No new choice beyond the declared sources.

items.title: Positive-characteristic Specht head and cyclotomic crystal labels agree
items.statement: In the positive-characteristic nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized cellular head dotD(lambda) for each restricted partition lambda is isomorphic, with shift zero, to the normalized simple of the same right crystal label lambda. The reduction J(lambda) of the characteristic-zero normalized simple contains that crystal-labelled simple once, and has no constituents with cellular labels not dominated by lambda. Its G0 class is invariant under finite-module diagram duality. This proves the CP label comparison needed for the crystal-labelled adjustment matrix; it is not a positive-characteristic global-basis identification.
items.strategy:
Now let J(lambda) be the reduction of the characteristic-zero normalized simple of crystal label lambda, constructed using a rational Specht-generator lattice. Its graded word character equals that of the characteristic-zero simple. Choose an extremal word of this common character. In characteristic zero the reconstruction label is lambda; in positive characteristic the same word gives the same canonical B(Lambda) label. The displayed quotient is1 for the characteristic-zero simple, hence [J(lambda):D_crystal(lambda)]_q=1 in positive characteristic.

Independently, the corrected canonical Fock comparison and the upper expansion identify [J(lambda)] with the inverse image of the characteristic-zero upper vector. The restricted upper-transition minor is dominance-unitriangular. Invert it over Z[q,q^{-1}] and use the ACTUAL positive-characteristic cellular-head triangular expansion of restricted Specht classes. This gives [J(lambda)]=[D_cell(lambda)]+sum_{nu<lambda}a_nu(q)[D_cell(nu)]. These coefficients are the actual composition multiplicities because J(lambda) is a module; there is no asserted positivity from matrix inversion alone. Induct over a finite dominance refinement in the fixed root degree. Assume D_cell(nu)=D_crystal(nu) for the smaller labels. Since different crystal labels give different simple orbits, D_crystal(lambda) cannot be any smaller D_cell(nu). Its occurrence in J(lambda) therefore forces D_cell(lambda)=D_crystal(lambda). The coefficient1 forces shift0 as both chosen representatives are self-dual. This proves the CP label comparison before defining adjustment polynomials in the crystal-labelled basis.

The characteristic-zero simple D(lambda) is normalized for finite vector duality, so each word component e(nu)D(lambda) has a symmetric graded dimension: its Laurent polynomial is unchanged by v -> v^{-1}. The constructed J(lambda) has exactly the same graded word character. The descended generator-fixing anti-involution fixes every word idempotent; hence e(nu)D_psi J(lambda) is the graded vector dual of e(nu)J(lambda), and its graded dimension is the same symmetric polynomial. Therefore D_psi J(lambda) and J(lambda) have identical word characters. The completed local extremal-word character detection proves G0 character injectivity over the actual positive-characteristic field, so [D_psi J(lambda)]=[J(lambda)]. This proves bar invariance of its CLASS; no self-dual stable integral lattice is asserted.

items.title: The graded adjustment polynomials in positive characteristic
items.statement:
In branch (CP) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the reduced modules $J(
u)$ of [[lem-reduction-of-characteristic-zero-simple-modules-modulo-p]] and the normalized simples $D(\lambda)$ with crystal label $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$ of the general-field normalization/crystal clauses of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] and [[lem-positive-characteristic-specht-head-and-cyclotomic-crystal-labels-agree]] (in branch (C0) these are the heads of the graded Specht modules by [[thm-graded-specht-heads-classify-the-graded-simple-modules]] (3)), define the **graded adjustment polynomials** $a_{\lambda,
u}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ for $\lambda,
u\in RP_\alpha$ by $$[J(
u)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,
u}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,
u}(q)=[J(
u):D(\lambda)]_q .$$ Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,
u})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy $a_{
u,
u}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd
u$ (dominance); equivalently $a_{\lambda,
u}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in $(\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke})^{-1}(D_
u)$.

**Source comparison (recorded, not used).** For level one and $\xi=1$ the source states that this adjustment matrix specializes at $q=1$ to the adjustment matrix of James; that degenerate comparison lies outside the nondegenerate branch of this page and is deferred (see the batch coverage record). No choice is used in the definition.
items.strategy: Expand the actual finite-dimensional J(nu) in the shift-orbit basis of normalized positive-characteristic simples; this uniquely defines the Laurent coefficients and makes their coefficients nonnegative integers. The general-field cover/duality/crystal suppliers normalize these simples; the local CP head/crystal lemma identifies their labels with the cellular-head labels, without using the characteristic-zero-only global theorem in CP. The local CP comparison proves J(nu)=D(nu)+terms with smaller labels, giving diagonal1 and dominance support. Bar invariance follows from WORD CHARACTERS: the characteristic-zero normalized simple is finite-dual self-dual, so each word graded dimension is symmetric in q. J(nu) has this same character, and D_psi J(nu) has the inverted character, hence the same one. The actual extremal-word character detection implies equality of their G0 classes. Applying duality to the expansion fixes every normalized simple and inverts q, so uniqueness gives a(q)=a(q^-1). No self-dual stable integral lattice, field-bar compatibility of an unspecified form, or positive-characteristic global-basis theorem is assumed. The source's degenerate comparison remains recorded outside this page's parameter branch. No new choice.

items.title: Canonical bases do not solve arbitrary positive-characteristic decomposition numbers
items.statement: The characteristic-zero theorems of this page ([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]) compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization [[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]] reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the boundary recorded in [[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]] and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
items.strategy: Compare exactly what the two cited results determine: the characteristic-zero identifications compute $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$ as $d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$, while the positive-characteristic factorization leaves the adjustment coefficients $a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)$ undetermined beyond bar-invariance, nonnegativity, unitriangularity and the dominance support of [[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]. The source's announced specialization to James's matrix concerns the degenerate parameter and is outside this page's regime (recorded in the coverage). No claim of a general positive-characteristic formula is made. Provenance: statement literature-derived; the remark is not consumed to prove any replacement.

items.title: Projective and simple Grothendieck classes in a small non-semisimple block
items.statement: Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$. Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e. $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ with $t=T_1+1$, a local algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$ convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so $$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$ The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and $\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence under the transported identifications of [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] $$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$ The graded Cartan pairing of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). Thus the projective class $[P]$ is not a simple class, and the two bases are dual to each other under $h$ without being equal as classes. All computations are finite and explicit; choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited.
items.strategy: Compute in the algebra: $T_1^2=(\xi-1)T_1+\xi=-2T_1-1$ gives $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ is local with radical $(t)$ and unique simple $D=\mathbb C$, and the regular module is the unique indecomposable projective because a local algebra has a unique simple and its regular module is projective; the graded composition series follows from $tP\cong D\{2\}$ (multiplication by $t$ shifts degree by $2$) and $P\cong D\oplus tP$ as graded vector spaces. The block statement uses the residue-content computation: nodes of $(2)$ have residues $0,1$ and nodes of $(1,1)$ have residues $0,-1\equiv1$, so both lie in the block of content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1=\alpha_1+\alpha_0$; the transported grading is [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock identities are the explicit $e=2$ computation of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] (its recorded $e=2$ example), the graded Specht degrees are read from the degree recursion of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] (the unique tableau of $(2)$ has degree $d_A(2)=1$: the addable $1$-node $(2,1)$ lies strictly below the removable node $(1,2)$, and there is no removable $1$-node below it), and the projective/simple identifications are [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]. The pairing values are read from $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,D)=\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,P)=1+q^2$ (endomorphisms are the identity and multiplication by $t$, of degree $2$). No choice.

items.title: Specializing the grading variable to one forgets graded decomposition information
items.statement:
The claim under refutation is that specializing the grading variable $q$ to
$1$ determines the graded decomposition data: that the forgetful map is
injective on the graded Grothendieck classes of the block, or equivalently that
the graded transition polynomials, graded Cartan entries and shift classes are
recovered from their values at $q=1$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The rank-two $e=2$ block of the example and the grading variable $q$.

[F1] In the example's block $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$, $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, with the graded Cartan pairing and shift action there recorded
([[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]]).

[F2] The level-one transition polynomials in the $e=2$ case are $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}(q)=1$ and $d_{(1,1),(2)}(q)=q$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]).

[F3] The graded decomposition theorem identifies the graded multiplicities with the transition polynomials
([[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The polynomials and the class $[P]$.** In $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ the elements $1+q^2$ and $2$ differ (their difference $q^2-1$ is nonzero) while $(1+q^2)|_{q=1}=2$; multiplying by the nonzero class $[D]$ gives distinct classes $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ and $2[D]$ in the free $A$-module $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1})$, whose images under the forgetful map $\zeta$ (which satisfies $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$) both equal $2[D]$ [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] [F1]. [F1]

1.2 **The Specht classes and the transition polynomials.** The example computes $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, which are distinct because $q\ne1$; the forgetful map sends both to $[D]$. The corresponding transition polynomials are $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}(q)=1$ and $d_{(1,1),(2)}(q)=q$ in the recorded $e=2$ Fock computation, distinct in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and equal at $q=1$ ([[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]], [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]) [F2]. [F1, F2]

2.1 **Conclusion.** By the graded decomposition theorem the classes are read through the transition polynomials, so the failure above is exactly the statement that the specialization $q\mapsto1$ loses the graded multiplicities and shift data ([[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]). All computations are finite evaluations in the rank-two block and use no choice. [F1, F2, F3] ∎
